quiz.explain: The fewer parts a whole has, the bigger each part. 1/4 is biggest.
steps: All pieces are 1 part of the same whole.
Fewer parts means bigger pieces: 4 parts is the fewest here.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a bigger bottom number means a bigger piece

quiz.q: How many 1/5 pieces join to make a whole strip?
quiz.explain: 5 fifths make a whole.
steps: Each piece is 1/5 of the strip.

quiz.q: Which is smaller: 1/3 or 1/10 of the same strip?
quiz.explain: A strip cut into 10 parts has smaller pieces than one cut into 3.
steps: One strip is cut into 3 parts, the other into 10.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 10 is bigger so 1/10 is bigger

quiz.q: Which list is in order from smallest to biggest?
quiz.explain: 1/8 is the smallest piece and 1/2 is the biggest.
steps: For 1 part of a whole: more parts means a smaller piece.
1/8 is the smallest, then 1/4, then 1/2 is the biggest.
quiz.mistake: Orders by the bottom numbers only

quiz.q: Which sign is correct? 1/6 ☐ 1/5
quiz.explain: 1/6 is smaller than 1/5 because 6 parts are smaller than 5 parts of the same whole.
steps: 1/6 is 1 of 6 parts; 1/5 is 1 of 5 parts of the same whole.
Cutting into 6 parts makes smaller pieces than cutting into 5.

quiz.q: In a fraction kit, how many 1/8 strips are as long as the whole strip?
quiz.explain: 8 eighths make the whole.
steps: Each 1/8 strip is 1 of 8 equal parts.
So 8 strips are as long as the whole.

quiz.q: Ria cuts one strip into 3 equal parts and another equal strip into 7 equal parts. Which parts are bigger?
quiz.explain: Fewer parts means bigger parts. 1/3 > 1/7.
steps: Both strips are the same size.
Cutting into 3 parts makes bigger pieces than cutting into 7.
quiz.mistake: Thinks more parts means bigger parts

quiz.q: Which fraction is between 1/3 and 1/5 in size?
quiz.explain: 1/3 > 1/4 > 1/5, so 1/4 is between them.
steps: 1/3 and 1/5: a fraction between them has a bottom number between 3 and 5.
1/8 and 1/6 are smaller than 1/5; 1/2 is bigger than 1/3.
quiz.mistake: Picks a fraction outside the range

teach.ask: Gappu has a fraction kit and asks which piece is bigger, 1/4 or 1/6. Explain.
teach.praise: 1/4 is bigger because the whole is cut into fewer parts!
teach.nudge: What happens to the piece size when the whole is cut into more parts?

revise.summary: A fraction kit has strips of the same whole cut into different numbers of equal parts. The more parts the whole is cut into, the smaller each part.
focus: Compare and order unit fractions
Count how many unit pieces make a whole strip
Use < and > with unit fractions
remember: Five 1/5 pieces make one whole strip
Only compare pieces of the same whole
traps: A bigger bottom number does not mean a bigger piece
Don't compare 6 and 5 directly: 1/6 < 1/5
Don't compare fractions of different wholes: half of a small roti may be less than a quarter of a big one

topics.title: Fractions of a group: my flower garden

learn.hook: A garden has 7 flowers: 3 roses and 4 marigolds. What fraction are roses?
points: A fraction can describe part of a group: 3 roses out of 7 flowers = 3/7.
The bottom number is the total number in the group. The top number is how many we are talking about.
In a garden plan, name the fraction for each flower type.
The fractions for all the parts of a group add up to one whole: 3/7 + 4/7 = 7/7 = 1.

example.q: A garden has 10 plants: 5 tulsi, 3 rose and 2 jasmine. What fraction is each type? Do they make a whole?

learn.reallife: In your class, the fraction of children wearing spectacles, or the fraction who like cricket, are fractions of a group!

games.title: Garden of 12 flowers: 6 roses, 4 lilies, 2 sunflowers

items.q: 2 of 8 laddoos are besan: besan fraction

quiz.q: A garden has 3 roses and 4 marigolds. What fraction of the flowers are roses?
quiz.explain: 3 roses out of 3 + 4 = 7 flowers is 3/7.
quiz.mistake: Uses the marigolds as the bottom number

quiz.q: In the same garden (3 roses, 4 marigolds), what fraction are marigolds?
quiz.explain: 4 marigolds out of 7 flowers is 4/7.
quiz.mistake: Puts the roses on the bottom

quiz.q: A garden plan has 9 beds: 2 rose, 3 lily, 4 marigold. What fraction are lily beds?
quiz.explain: 3 lily beds out of 9 is 3/9.

quiz.q: Gita wants a garden of 8 flowers where 5/8 are sunflowers. How many sunflowers should she plant?
quiz.explain: 5/8 of 8 flowers = 5 flowers.
steps: 5/8 of 8 flowers: make 8 equal groups of 1 flower each.

quiz.q: In Gita's 8-flower garden with 5 sunflowers, the rest are roses. What fraction are roses?
quiz.explain: 8 − 5 = 3 roses, so 3/8.

quiz.q: A garden has 4/10 roses and 3/10 lilies. The rest are tulips. What fraction are tulips?
quiz.mistake: Forgets that parts add to one whole

quiz.q: Do 2/6 + 1/6 + 3/6 make one whole?
steps: All are sixths, so add the top numbers: 2 + 1 + 3 = 6.
6/6 = 1, so Yes, they make one whole.

quiz.q: A basket has 12 fruits: 5 apples and the rest bananas. What fraction are bananas?
quiz.explain: 12 − 5 = 7 bananas, so 7/12.

teach.ask: Gappu's garden has 2 roses, 3 lilies and 1 sunflower. Help Gappu write the fractions.
teach.praise: 2/6 roses, 3/6 lilies, 1/6 sunflower, and together they make 6/6, one whole garden!
teach.nudge: What is the total number of flowers, and what do all the fractions add up to?

revise.summary: A fraction can describe part of a group: 3 roses out of 7 flowers is 3/7. The fractions for all the parts of a group add up to one whole.
focus: Write the fraction for each type in a group
Find the fraction of the rest
Check that all parts add to one whole
remember: Bottom: total number in the group. Top: how many we are talking about
traps: Don't use one type as the bottom number; use the total
Don't add the bottom numbers
Don't forget that all the parts of a group add to one whole

topics.title: Dosa toppings: fractions of a whole

learn.hook: One dosa, three toppings! 3/8 with potato, 1/8 with onion, 4/8 with paneer. Hungry yet?
points: Cut a round dosa into equal parts to show fractions of toppings.
Write a fraction for each topping: parts with that topping over total parts.
To make a dosa matching an order like 2/3 and 1/3, cut it into 3 equal parts: 2 parts one topping, 1 part another.
All the toppings together cover the whole dosa: 3/8 + 1/8 + 4/8 = 8/8 = 1.

example.q: An order says: 3/8 potato, 1/8 onion, 4/8 paneer. How many parts of each, and does it cover the whole dosa?
steps: Cut the dosa into 8 equal parts.

learn.reallife: At a dosa stall, a family may order one big dosa with different toppings for different people. Fractions help share it fairly!

items.text: Order 2/3 and 1/3: cut into ___ parts.
Order 3/8, 1/8, 4/8: paneer gets ___ parts.
Order 1/4 and 3/4: cut into ___ parts.

quiz.q: A dosa is cut into 4 equal parts. 3 parts have chutney. What fraction has chutney?
quiz.explain: 3 out of 4 equal parts: 3/4.
steps: The dosa has 4 equal parts; 3 have chutney.

quiz.q: An order says 2/3 masala and 1/3 plain. How many equal parts should the dosa be cut into?
quiz.explain: The bottom number is 3, so cut into 3 equal parts.
steps: The bottom number 3 tells the number of equal parts.
So cut the dosa into 3 equal parts.

quiz.q: A dosa has 3/8 potato and 1/8 onion. The rest is paneer. What fraction is paneer?
quiz.explain: 3/8 + 1/8 = 4/8. The whole is 8/8, so paneer is 8/8 − 4/8 = 4/8.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that the toppings make a whole

quiz.q: A dosa is cut into 6 equal parts: 1 part cheese, 2 parts onion, 3 parts plain. What fraction is onion?
quiz.explain: 2 out of 6 parts: 2/6.
steps: The dosa has 6 equal parts. Onion is on 2 parts.
Check: cheese 1/6 + onion 2/6 + plain 3/6 = 6/6, the whole dosa.
quiz.mistake: Uses the wrong number of parts

quiz.q: Which order covers the whole dosa?
quiz.explain: 2/5 + 3/5 = 5/5 = 1 whole. The others are less than a whole.
steps: A whole needs the top and bottom numbers to be equal.
quiz.mistake: Does not add the top numbers

quiz.q: Lata wants 1/4 cheese and 3/4 plain on her dosa. Cut into 4 parts, how many parts are plain?
quiz.explain: 3/4 means 3 of the 4 parts.
steps: The dosa is cut into 4 equal parts.
3/4 plain means 3 of the 4 parts are plain.
So 3 parts are plain (1 part is cheese).

quiz.q: A dosa has 5 equal parts. 2 have ghee. What fraction has NO ghee?
quiz.explain: 5 − 2 = 3 parts without ghee: 3/5.

quiz.q: A dosa is 3/8 potato, 1/8 onion and 4/8 paneer. Which topping covers the most?
quiz.explain: 4/8 is the biggest since all parts are eighths and 4 is the largest top number.
steps: All toppings are in eighths, so compare the top numbers.
4 is the biggest, so paneer (4/8) covers the most.

teach.ask: Gappu's family ordered one dosa: 2/3 masala and 1/3 plain. How should the cook make it?
teach.praise: Cut it into 3 equal parts: 2 masala, 1 plain. Yum!
teach.nudge: How many equal parts does the dosa need, and how many get masala?

revise.summary: Cut a round dosa into equal parts and write a fraction for each topping: parts with that topping over total parts. All the toppings together cover the whole dosa.
focus: Write the fraction for each topping
Cut a dosa to match an order
Find the missing topping fraction
remember: An order of 2/3 and 1/3: cut into 3 equal parts
traps: Cut by the bottom number; don't add 2 + 3
Don't forget that the toppings make a whole
Don't give the part with a topping when the part without it is asked

topics.title: Sharing a group: fractions of a collection

learn.hook: Dadi has 12 laddoos and says half are for you. How many is that? Let's share!
points: To find a fraction of a group, first make equal groups.
Half of 12: make 2 equal groups. Each group has 12 ÷ 2 = 6.
One quarter of 20: make 4 equal groups. Each group has 20 ÷ 4 = 5.
To find 3/4 of 16, find 1/4 first (16 ÷ 4 = 4), then take 3 groups: 3 × 4 = 12.
The bottom number tells how many groups to make. The top number tells how many groups to take.

example.q: Harpreet has 18 pencils. She gives 1/3 of them to Joseph. How many does she give, and how many are left?
steps: 1/3 is one group: she gives 6 pencils.

learn.reallife: Sharing sweets on Diwali, dividing marbles among friends or splitting a bill all use fractions of a group.

items.text: Half of 10 bangles is ___ bangles.
1/4 of 16 marbles is ___ marbles.
To find 1/3 of a group, make ___ equal groups.
3/4 of 20 kites is ___ kites.

quiz.q: Dadi has 12 laddoos. She gives half of them to Riya. How many laddoos does Riya get?
quiz.explain: Half means 2 equal groups. 12 ÷ 2 = 6.
quiz.mistake: Takes away 2 instead of dividing by 2

quiz.q: What is one quarter of 20 marbles?
quiz.explain: A quarter means 4 equal groups. 20 ÷ 4 = 5.
steps: One quarter of 20 marbles is 5 marbles.
quiz.mistake: Gives the number of groups (4) instead of the number in each group

quiz.q: What is 1/3 of 15 mangoes?
quiz.explain: Make 3 equal groups. 15 ÷ 3 = 5 in each group.

quiz.q: What is 3/4 of 16 diyas?
quiz.explain: 1/4 of 16 is 4. 3/4 is three of those groups: 3 × 4 = 12.

quiz.q: Harpreet has 18 pencils. She gives 1/3 of them to Joseph. How many pencils does Harpreet have left?
quiz.explain: 1/3 of 18 is 6, which she gives away. 18 - 6 = 12 are left.
quiz.mistake: Gives the part given away instead of the part left

quiz.q: Kabir has ₹40. He spends 1/4 of it on a kite. How much does the kite cost?
steps: 1/4 of ₹40 means split ₹40 into 4 equal parts.
quiz.mistake: Finds half (₹20) instead of a quarter

quiz.q: What is 2/5 of 25 laddoos?
Joseph shares 24 grapes equally among 4 friends. What fraction of the grapes does each friend get?
quiz.explain: Each friend gets 1 of 4 equal shares, so each gets 1/4 of the grapes. (That is 6 grapes.)
steps: The grapes are shared equally among 4 friends: 4 equal shares.
Each friend gets 1 of the 4 shares = 1/4.
(That is 24 ÷ 4 = 6 grapes, but the question asks for the fraction: 1/4.)
quiz.mistake: Gives the number of grapes (6) instead of the fraction

teach.ask: Gappu has 20 seeds and wants to give 1/4 of them to a friend. How many seeds should Gappu give?
teach.praise: Yes! Make 4 equal groups and give 1 group: 5 seeds. Gappu's friend is happy!
teach.nudge: How many equal groups should Gappu make for a quarter?

revise.summary: To find a fraction of a group, first make equal groups. The bottom number tells how many groups to make and the top number tells how many groups to take.
focus: Find half, a quarter and a third of a group
Find fractions like 3/4 or 2/5 of a number
Find how many are left after giving a fraction away
remember: Half of 12: 12 ÷ 2 = 6. One quarter of 20: 20 ÷ 4 = 5
traps: Don't take away 2 instead of dividing by 2
Don't find only 1/4 and stop when 3/4 is asked
Don't give the part given away when the part left is asked

learn.hook: Half a glass of milk, a quarter of an hour, one-third of a class... fractions are everywhere!
points: To show 1/3 of a set, draw the set in 3 equal groups and circle one group.
To show 1/5 of a set, draw 5 equal groups and circle one.
To split 16 sweets into 4 equal parts, each part has 16 ÷ 4 = 4 sweets.
We use fractions every day: half a litre of milk, quarter past three, half price sale, a third of the class.

example.q: Draw to show 1/3 of 12 bangles.
steps: Make 3 equal groups of the 12 bangles.

learn.reallife: A cricket match has 2 innings, each half of the match. A pizza in 8 slices shows eighths!

games.title: Is a fraction used here?
items: One-third of the class went on a trip

quiz.q: 16 sweets are split into 4 equal parts. How many sweets in each part?
steps: Split 16 sweets into 4 equal parts: divide.

quiz.q: To show 1/3 of 15 balloons, how many equal groups should you draw?
quiz.explain: The bottom number 3 tells how many equal groups to make.
steps: In 1/3, the bottom number tells how many equal groups to make.
So draw 3 equal groups (5 balloons in each).
quiz.mistake: Uses the number in each group

quiz.q: What is 1/5 of 10 pencils? Show it by grouping.
quiz.explain: 10 pencils in 5 equal groups gives 2 in each group.

quiz.q: Which is a real-life use of a fraction?
options: Buying half a kilogram of tomatoes
quiz.explain: Half a kilogram is 1/2 kg, a fraction.
steps: A fraction is a part of a whole.
Page 20 and 7 birds are whole numbers, so the answer is buying half a kilogram of tomatoes.
Answer: Buying half a kilogram of tomatoes

quiz.q: 'The school bus will come at quarter past 7.' Which fraction is in this sentence?
quiz.explain: Quarter past means 1/4 of an hour, which is 15 minutes, after 7.
steps: Quarter past 7 means 1/4 of an hour after 7.
quiz.mistake: Does not see 'quarter' as a fraction

quiz.q: Mili draws 12 stars and circles 1/3 of them. How many stars are circled?
A class of 30 children: 1/5 come by bus. How many come by bus?
Ravi splits 16 sweets so that his 4 friends get 1/4 each. How many does each friend get?

teach.ask: Gappu wants to show 1/5 of 20 grains on paper. How should Gappu draw it?
teach.praise: 5 equal groups of 4, and I circle one group. 1/5 of 20 is 4!
teach.nudge: How many equal groups do you draw, and how many are in one group?

revise.summary: To show 1/3 of a set, draw it in 3 equal groups and circle one group. We use fractions every day, like half a litre of milk or quarter past three.
focus: Show a fraction of a set by grouping
Find a unit fraction of a number
Spot fractions in everyday life
remember: The bottom number tells how many equal groups to draw
16 sweets in 4 equal parts: 16 ÷ 4 = 4
Quarter past means 1/4 of an hour (15 minutes)
traps: Don't subtract instead of dividing
Don't give the number of groups instead of the number in each group
Don't circle 3 stars for 1/3 of 12; circle 4

learn.hook: Mummy asks for 'half a kilo of tomatoes' and 'a quarter litre of milk'. Fractions help us measure!
points: 1 metre = 100 cm, so 1/2 metre = 50 cm and 1/4 metre = 25 cm.
1 kilogram = 1000 g, so 1/2 kg = 500 g and 1/4 kg = 250 g.
1 litre = 1000 ml, so 1/2 litre = 500 ml and 3/4 litre = 750 ml.
1 hour = 60 minutes, so half an hour = 30 minutes and a quarter of an hour = 15 minutes.
To find 3/4 of a measure, find 1/4 first, then multiply by 3.

example.q: How many centimetres is 3/4 of a metre?

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers sell ½ kg of sugar, milkmen pour ½ litre, and tailors cut ¼ metre of lace.

games.title: Match the fraction to the measure

quiz.q: How many centimetres are there in half a metre?
quiz.explain: 1 metre = 100 cm. Half of 100 cm is 50 cm.
quiz.mistake: Uses 1000 instead of 100 for a metre, or finds a quarter

quiz.q: How many grams is 1/4 kg?
quiz.mistake: Uses 100 g for a kilogram (gets 25 g)

quiz.q: Aisha buys 1/2 litre of milk. How many millilitres is that?
quiz.explain: 1 litre = 1000 ml. Half of 1000 ml is 500 ml.

quiz.q: How many minutes are there in a quarter of an hour?
quiz.explain: 1 hour = 60 minutes. 60 ÷ 4 = 15 minutes.

quiz.q: How many centimetres is 3/4 of a metre?
Meena buys 2 packets of sugar. Each packet is 1/2 kg. How much sugar is that?
quiz.explain: Two halves make one whole. 1/2 kg + 1/2 kg = 1 kg.

quiz.q: Which is heavier: 1/2 kg of rice or 300 g of dal?
quiz.explain: 1/2 kg = 500 g, and 500 g is more than 300 g. So the rice is heavier.
quiz.mistake: Sees 300 is bigger than 1/2 and forgets to change kg to g

quiz.q: Joseph has a 1 m ribbon. He cuts it into 4 equal pieces. How long is each piece?
quiz.explain: Each piece is 1/4 of a metre. 100 cm ÷ 4 = 25 cm.
quiz.mistake: Gives the number of pieces as the length

teach.ask: The shopkeeper gave Gappu 500 g of peanuts when Gappu asked for half a kilo. Was Gappu cheated?
teach.praise: Phew! 1 kg is 1000 g, and half of 1000 is 500. The shopkeeper was fair. Thank you!
teach.nudge: How many grams are there in 1 kg? What is half of that?

revise.summary: Fractions help us measure: 1/2 metre is 50 cm, 1/2 kg is 500 g, 1/2 litre is 500 ml and half an hour is 30 minutes. To find 3/4 of a measure, find 1/4 first, then multiply by 3.
focus: Change fractions of a metre, kilogram, litre and hour into smaller units
Find 3/4 of a measure
Compare measures after changing units
remember: 1 litre = 1000 ml; 3/4 litre = 750 ml
1 hour = 60 minutes; a quarter of an hour = 15 minutes
traps: Don't use 100 g for a kilogram or 100 ml for a litre
An hour has 60 minutes, not 100
Don't compare kg and g directly: 1/2 kg = 500 g, which is more than 300 g

learn.hook: Fold a paper in half, then in half again. One half is now two quarters. Same paper, new name!
points: Fold a paper into 3 equal parts, then fold in half again. You get 6 parts, and 1/3 = 2/6.
Equivalent fractions name the same amount using a different number of parts.
To make an equivalent fraction, multiply the top and bottom by the same number: 1/3 = 2/6 (both × 2).

example.q: A paper is folded in half 3 times. How many parts are there, and how many show one half?
steps: Fold 1: 2 parts. Fold 2: 4 parts. Fold 3: 8 parts.
Half the paper is 4 of the 8 parts.

learn.reallife: Half a pizza cut into 4 slices is the same as half a pizza cut into 2 big slices. Same amount, different number of pieces!

games.title: Same amount?
items: Each third folded in half gives 2 sixths.
2/4 is a half, which is bigger than a quarter.

quiz.q: A paper folded into thirds is then folded in half. How many sixths are in one third?
quiz.explain: Each third is split into 2, so 1/3 = 2/6.
steps: Folding into thirds makes 3 parts. Folding in half splits each third into 2.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the third stays as 1 part

quiz.q: Which fraction is equivalent to 1/2?
quiz.explain: 4/8: 4 is half of 8.
steps: A fraction equal to 1/2 has a top number that is half the bottom number.
quiz.mistake: Picks a fraction with a 2 in it

quiz.explain: Each time the bottom doubles, the top doubles: 4 × 2 = 8.
steps: Look at the bottoms: 2, 4, 8, 16 — doubling each time.

quiz.q: What does 'equivalent fractions' mean?
options: Fractions with the same top number
Fractions that name the same amount
Fractions with the same bottom number
quiz.explain: Equivalent fractions show the same amount in different ways.
steps: Equivalent fractions name the same amount, written in different ways.
Answer: Fractions that name the same amount
quiz.mistake: Thinks the numbers must look the same

quiz.q: Which is equivalent to 1/3?
quiz.explain: Multiply top and bottom by 2: 1/3 = 2/6.
steps: Multiply the top and the bottom of 1/3 by 2.
3/6 = 1/2 and 2/3 is bigger, so the answer is 2/6.

quiz.q: Rina folds a paper in half 2 times and colours 2 parts. What fraction is coloured?
quiz.explain: 2 folds make 4 parts. 2 of 4 = 2/4 = 1/2.
steps: Folding in half once makes 2 parts; folding again makes 4 parts.

quiz.explain: 8 is 4 × 2, so the top is 1 × 2 = 2.
steps: Do the same to the top: 1 × 2 = 2.

quiz.q: Which pair is NOT equivalent?
quiz.explain: 3/6 is a half, but 1/3 is less than a half. So they are not equal.

teach.ask: Gappu thinks 2/4 is bigger than 1/2 because it has bigger numbers. Show Gappu with paper folding.
teach.praise: I folded my paper and 2 quarters cover the same as 1 half! They are equivalent.
teach.nudge: What do you see when you fold a half in half again?

revise.summary: Equivalent fractions name the same amount using a different number of parts. To make one, multiply the top and bottom by the same number.
focus: Find equivalent fractions by folding
Fill the missing number in equivalent fractions
Spot pairs that are not equivalent
traps: Don't multiply only the bottom number
Don't add 2 each time; double both numbers
1/3 and 3/6 are not equivalent: 3/6 is a half

learn.hook: A fraction chart lines up halves, thirds, quarters, sixths, eighths and tenths. It is a map of fractions!
points: A fraction chart shows the same whole as rows of 1/2s, 1/3s, 1/4s, 1/6s, 1/8s and 1/10s.
Two 1/4s cover 1/2. Two 1/8s cover 1/4. Ten 1/10s make a whole.
Use the chart to compare: 2/3 is longer than 1/2, so 2/3 > 1/2.
Check if two combinations are equal: three 1/6s = 1/2 but two 1/8s = 1/4, so they are not equal.
Smaller pieces can combine into a bigger piece: two 1/6s make 1/3; two 1/10s make 1/5.

example.q: Are three 1/6 pieces equal to two 1/8 pieces?

learn.reallife: When sharing laddoos cut into halves and quarters, a fraction chart helps check that everyone gets the same amount.

quiz.q: How many 1/4 pieces make 1/2?
quiz.explain: On the chart, two quarters cover one half.
steps: On the fraction chart, put quarters under the half.

quiz.q: How many 1/8 pieces make 1/4?
quiz.explain: Two eighths cover one quarter.
steps: Two eighths fit under one quarter.

quiz.q: How many 1/10 pieces make a whole?
quiz.explain: Ten tenths make one whole.
steps: Each tenth is 1 of 10 equal parts.

quiz.q: Which is bigger: 2/3 or 1/2?
quiz.explain: On the chart, 2/3 reaches further than 1/2.
steps: 2/3 = 1/3 + 1/3. On the chart, it reaches past the half mark.

quiz.q: Is three 1/6s the same as two 1/8s?
quiz.explain: Three 1/6s = 1/2 and two 1/8s = 1/4. 1/2 is more.
steps: 1/2 is more than 1/4, so three 1/6s is more.
quiz.mistake: Compares only the number of pieces

quiz.q: Which smaller pieces combine to make exactly 1/3?
quiz.mistake: Picks pieces that do not fit

quiz.q: How many 1/8 pieces make 1/2?
quiz.explain: Two 1/8s make 1/4, and two 1/4s make 1/2. So 4 eighths make a half.

quiz.q: Which is equal to 1 whole?
quiz.explain: 6 sixths = 6/6 = 1 whole.
steps: A whole needs the number of pieces to equal the bottom number.
Seven 1/8s = 7/8; three 1/4s = 3/4; five 1/6s = 5/6: all less than 1.
quiz.mistake: Does not check that pieces fill the whole

teach.ask: Gappu has three 1/6 pieces and Bubbly has two 1/8 pieces. Gappu says they are equal. Use a fraction chart to check.
teach.praise: Three sixths cover a half, but two eighths cover only a quarter. Mine is more!
teach.nudge: What do three 1/6s cover on the chart, and what do two 1/8s cover?

revise.summary: A fraction chart shows the same whole as rows of halves, thirds, quarters, sixths, eighths and tenths. Use it to compare fractions and check if combinations are equal.
focus: Find how many smaller pieces make a bigger piece
Compare fractions using the chart
Check if two combinations are equal
remember: Two 1/4s cover 1/2. Two 1/8s cover 1/4. Ten 1/10s make a whole
Two 1/6s make 1/3; two 1/10s make 1/5
traps: 4 quarters do not make a half; 2 do
Don't compare only the number of pieces: three 1/6s = 1/2 but two 1/8s = 1/4
2 eighths make a quarter, not a half

learn.hook: Riya says her shape is 1/4 shaded. But are the parts equal? Let's be fraction detectives!
points: Before naming a fraction, check that the shape is cut into EQUAL parts.
Write the fraction as shaded parts over total equal parts.
If a claim like 'this is 1/4' is wrong because parts are unequal, add lines to make equal parts, then count again.
To shade a fraction, divide the shape into the number of equal parts on the bottom, then shade the top number of parts.

example.q: A square is cut into 2 equal rectangles. One rectangle is cut into 2 equal halves and one of those is shaded. Riya says 1/3 is shaded. Is she right?
steps: The square has 3 pieces, but they are not equal.
Cut the other rectangle in half too: now 4 equal parts.

learn.reallife: When you colour a chocolate bar picture in your notebook, check the pieces are equal before writing the fraction!

games.title: Detective check
items: A square split into 4 equal triangles with 1 shaded shows 1/4.
A shape split into 3 unequal parts with 1 shaded always shows 1/3.
To show 3/5, divide into 5 equal parts and shade 3.
A circle with 8 equal slices and 6 shaded shows 6/8.
Adding lines can turn unequal parts into equal ones.
Splitting the bigger parts makes them match.

quiz.q: A square is cut into 9 equal small squares. 4 are coloured. What fraction is coloured?
quiz.explain: 4 coloured out of 9 equal parts: 4/9.
steps: The square has 9 equal parts; 4 are coloured.

quiz.q: A rectangle has 3 parts: one big half and two small quarters. One quarter is shaded. What fraction is shaded?
quiz.explain: The parts are not equal. Split the half into 2 quarters: 4 equal parts, 1 shaded = 1/4.
steps: The parts are not equal, so first make equal parts.
Split the big half into 2 quarters: now 4 equal quarters.

quiz.q: To show 5/8 of a circle, what should you do?
options: Cut into 5 equal parts and shade 8
Cut into 8 equal parts and shade 5
quiz.explain: Bottom number 8 gives the equal parts; top number 5 gives how many to shade.
steps: In 5/8, the bottom number 8 gives the number of equal parts.
The top number 5 gives how many to shade.
So cut into 8 equal parts and shade 5.
Answer: Cut into 8 equal parts and shade 5

quiz.q: Rohan says a shape cut into 4 unequal parts with 1 shaded shows 1/4. What is wrong?
quiz.explain: Fractions need equal parts. Unequal parts cannot show 1/4.
steps: A fraction like 1/4 needs 4 EQUAL parts.
So the shading does not show 1/4: the parts are not equal.
Answer: The parts are not equal
quiz.mistake: Ignores the size of the parts

quiz.q: A strip has 10 equal parts. 3 are red and 2 are blue. What fraction is coloured?
quiz.explain: 3 + 2 = 5 coloured parts out of 10: 5/10.

quiz.q: A hexagon is split into 6 equal triangles. 2 are shaded. What fraction is NOT shaded?
quiz.explain: 6 − 2 = 4 not shaded: 4/6.
steps: The hexagon has 6 equal triangles; 2 are shaded.

quiz.q: How should you divide a square to shade 1/4 of it?
quiz.explain: 1/4 means 1 of 4 equal parts.
steps: So divide the square into 4 equal parts.

quiz.q: A circle has 12 equal parts. 9 are shaded. What fraction is shaded?
quiz.explain: 9 of 12 equal parts: 9/12.
steps: The circle has 12 equal parts; 9 are shaded.

teach.ask: Gappu coloured 1 piece of a shape with 3 unequal pieces and wrote 1/3. Help Gappu fix it.
teach.praise: First make the parts equal by adding lines, then count. Now my fraction is right!
teach.nudge: Are the pieces equal? What could you do to make them equal?

revise.summary: Before naming a fraction, check the shape is cut into EQUAL parts, then write shaded parts over total equal parts. If parts are unequal, add lines to make equal parts and count again.
focus: Write the shaded or unshaded fraction
Fix wrong claims when parts are unequal
Shade a given fraction
remember: Fraction = shaded parts over total equal parts
To shade a fraction: divide into the bottom number of equal parts, shade the top number
traps: Don't count unequal parts
Don't swap the top and bottom numbers
Count every colour that is shaded, not just one

topics.title: What do we measure, and with what?

learn.hook: How tall is the tree? How heavy is the watermelon? How hot is the tea? Each question measures something different!
points: We measure many things: length (how long), height (how tall), breadth (how wide), depth (how deep), weight (how heavy) and temperature (how hot or cold).
Length, height, breadth and depth are all measured in units of length, like cm and m.
A ruler or scale (15 cm or 30 cm) measures small things like a pencil.
A metre stick measures 1 m at a time, good for a table or a door.
A measuring tape rolls up and can measure long or curved things, like a room or your waist.

example.q: Which tool is best to measure the length of the classroom?
steps: A classroom is many metres long.
A 30 cm scale would need too many moves.
A long measuring tape is best.

learn.reallife: Tailors use a soft measuring tape, carpenters use a metal tape, and you use a scale in your geometry box!

quiz.q: 'How deep is the well?' asks about which measurement?
quiz.explain: How deep means depth, the distance down.
steps: 'How deep' asks how far down something goes.
Height is how tall, so the answer is Depth.

quiz.q: Which tool is best to measure the length of a pencil?
quiz.explain: A pencil is short, so a small scale works best.
steps: A pencil is short, only a few centimetres long.
A 15 cm scale is small and measures length.
A 30 m tape is too long; a weighing scale and thermometer don't measure length.
quiz.mistake: Picks a tool that does not measure length

quiz.q: A tailor measures the round waist of a customer. Which tool does she use?
quiz.explain: A soft tape can bend around curved things.
steps: A waist is round and curved.
A soft measuring tape can bend around curved things.
A stiff scale or metre stick cannot, so she uses a soft tape.
quiz.mistake: Picks a stiff tool for a curved shape

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a measure of length?
quiz.explain: Temperature tells how hot or cold, not how long.
steps: Depth, height and breadth are all lengths: how deep, how tall, how wide.
Temperature tells how hot or cold something is.
So temperature is NOT a measure of length.

quiz.q: 'How wide is the window?' Which word is used for how wide something is?
quiz.explain: How wide is the breadth.
steps: How wide something is, is its breadth.
Height is how tall; depth is how deep.

quiz.q: A metre stick is how long?
quiz.explain: A metre stick is 1 m, which is 100 cm.
steps: A metre stick is 1 m long.
So a metre stick is 100 cm long.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up metre and 30 cm scale

quiz.q: Ramu wants to know how hot his milk is. What does he measure?
quiz.explain: Hot or cold is temperature.
steps: How hot or cold something is, is its temperature.
Weight, depth and length do not tell hotness.

quiz.q: Which is the best tool to measure the length of the school corridor?
quiz.explain: A long corridor needs a long measuring tape.
steps: A school corridor is many metres long.
A 10 cm thread, 30 cm ruler or 15 cm scale is too short.
A long measuring tape is best.

teach.ask: Gappu wants to measure his classroom with his little 15 cm scale. Suggest what to measure with which tool.
teach.praise: Scale for small things, tape for long things! The classroom needs a tape.
teach.nudge: Which tool suits long things and which suits small things?

revise.summary: We measure length, height, breadth, depth, weight and temperature. Length, height, breadth and depth use units like cm and m, measured with a scale, a metre stick or a measuring tape.
focus: Match words like how deep, how wide and how tall to the right measurement
Choose the best tool to measure a length
Tell which measurements are not lengths
remember: Depth: how deep. Breadth: how wide. Height: how tall
Scale (15 cm or 30 cm) for small things; metre stick for 1 m at a time; measuring tape for long or curved things
A metre stick is 1 m = 100 cm
traps: Don't mix up depth and height, or breadth and height
Temperature and weight are not lengths
Don't use a stiff tool for a curved shape like a waist

topics.title: Feeling a metre: jumps and the classroom

learn.hook: Walk 1 metre, jump 5 metres, crawl 10 metres! How do they feel?
points: 1 m is about one big step of a grown-up. 5 m is about 5 big steps. 10 m is twice 5 m.
In a long jump contest, measure each jump with a rope or tape and write it in a table.
The longest jump has the biggest number; the shortest has the smallest.
Estimate first (a smart guess), then measure the length and breadth of the classroom to check.

example.q: Long jumps: Asha 2 m 10 cm, Babu 1 m 85 cm, Chetan 2 m 25 cm. Who jumped the longest?

learn.reallife: On sports day, long jump results are written on a board in metres and centimetres to pick the winner.

items.q: 10 m is how many 1 m lengths?
Classroom 8 m long, 6 m wide: length − breadth

quiz.q: Long jumps: Ravi 210 cm, Sita 185 cm, Tara 225 cm. Who jumped the shortest?
quiz.explain: 185 is the smallest, so Sita's jump was shortest.
steps: The jumps are 210 cm, 185 cm and 225 cm.
The shortest jump is the smallest number: 185.

quiz.q: In the same contest, how much longer was Tara's jump than Sita's?
steps: Tara jumped 225 cm; Sita jumped 185 cm.

quiz.q: Naren marks 10 m on the ground. How many 1 m lengths is that?
quiz.explain: 10 m is ten lengths of 1 m.
steps: 10 m means ten lengths of 1 m each.
So it is 10 lengths of 1 m.

quiz.q: Jaya guessed her classroom is 10 m long. She measured 8 m. How far off was her guess?
A classroom is 9 m long and 7 m wide. How much longer is its length than its breadth?
A child crawls 5 m, then walks another 5 m. How far did the child go?
steps: The child goes 5 m and then 5 m more.

quiz.q: Why do we write each jump in a table?
options: To compare jumps and find the longest and shortest
quiz.explain: A table keeps all the measurements in one place so we can compare them.
steps: A table puts all the jumps in one place.
Then we can easily compare them.
So we can find the longest and shortest jumps.
Answer: To compare jumps and find the longest and shortest
quiz.mistake: Does not see the use of a table

quiz.q: Jumps: Mohan 1 m 95 cm, Leena 2 m. Who jumped longer and by how much?
quiz.explain: 2 m = 200 cm. 200 − 195 = 5 cm. Leena jumped longer.

teach.ask: Gappu jumped 1 m 80 cm and Bubbly jumped 2 m 5 cm. Gappu thinks 80 is bigger, so he won. Help Gappu.
teach.praise: 180 cm and 205 cm! Bubbly jumped further. I must change everything to cm first.
teach.nudge: What happens if you change both jumps to centimetres?

revise.summary: 1 m is about one big step of a grown-up. In a long jump contest, measure each jump, write it in a table and compare: the longest jump has the biggest number.
focus: Find the longest and shortest jump from a table
Find how much longer one length is than another
Estimate first, then measure to check
remember: 1 m is about one big step of a grown-up
2 m = 200 cm, so 2 m is 5 cm more than 1 m 95 cm
traps: Don't pick the longest when the shortest is asked
Don't add when 'how much longer' or 'how far off' is asked
Don't compare m and cm without first changing m to cm

topics.title: Guess the length from what you know

learn.hook: A bus is 10 m long. A crocodile is half as long as the bus. How long is the crocodile?
points: If you know the length of one thing, you can work out others from it.
Half as long means divide by 2. Twice as long means multiply by 2.
When things are stacked one on top of another, add their heights.
Compare a stacked height with another length by adding first, then comparing.

example.q: A cricket bat is about 1 m long. A whale is about 25 bats long. About how long is the whale?

learn.reallife: Wildlife books often say things like 'an ostrich is taller than a man' or 'a blue whale is as long as 3 buses'.

games.title: Taller or longer?
items: A 70 cm table with a 40 cm box on it is taller than 1 m.
Half of a 12 m bus is 24 m.
Two 50 cm stools stacked are as tall as 1 m.
An ostrich 2 m tall is taller than a 150 cm child.
Three 30 cm books stacked are 1 m tall.

quiz.q: A bus is 12 m long. A crocodile is half as long. How long is the crocodile?
quiz.explain: Half of 12 m is 12 ÷ 2 = 6 m.
steps: Half as long means divide by 2.

quiz.q: An ostrich is 2 m tall. A giraffe is 3 times as tall. How tall is the giraffe?
steps: 3 times as tall means multiply by 3.

quiz.q: A cricket bat is 1 m. A whale is as long as 20 bats. How long is the whale?
steps: Each bat is 1 m; the whale is 20 bats long.

quiz.q: A stool is 45 cm tall. A box of 35 cm is put on it. How tall is the stack?
steps: The box sits on top of the stool, so add the heights.

quiz.q: A table is 75 cm tall. A pot of 30 cm is kept on it. Is the top of the pot higher than a 1 m stick standing next to it?
A snake is 3 m long. A lizard is 30 cm long. How many lizards laid end to end are as long as the snake?
quiz.mistake: Does not change m to cm

quiz.q: Three bricks, each 10 cm high, are stacked. How tall is the stack?
steps: 3 bricks, each 10 cm high, stacked → add or multiply.

quiz.q: A train coach is 20 m long. A car is 4 m long. How many cars fit along one coach?

teach.ask: Gappu knows a bus is 10 m long. Gappu wants to know how long a crocodile half the bus's length is. Explain.
teach.praise: Half of 10 m is 5 m! I can find lengths using things I already know.
teach.nudge: What does 'half as long' tell you to do?

revise.summary: If you know the length of one thing, you can work out others from it. Half as long means divide by 2, twice as long means multiply by 2, and stacked heights are added.
focus: Use half as long, twice as long and times as long
Add the heights of stacked things and compare
Find how many of one thing make another, after changing units
remember: Half as long: ÷ 2. Twice as long: × 2
Stacked one on another: add their heights
3 m = 300 cm, so 300 ÷ 30 = 10 lizards
traps: Don't double when the question says half
Don't add 3 when it says 3 times as tall
Don't divide m by cm; change m to cm first

learn.hook: Diwali lights, garlands and ribbons: how much do we need altogether? Let's add lengths!
points: To add or subtract lengths, first make the units the same.
If you get 100 cm or more, change 100 cm into 1 m: 125 cm = 1 m 25 cm.
To find how much longer, subtract the shorter length from the longer one.
To find how much is left after cutting, subtract the cut part.

example.q: Meena has a 75 cm ribbon and a 50 cm ribbon. What is their total length in m and cm?

learn.reallife: When you decorate for Diwali, you add up the lengths of light strings to see if they will cover the balcony.

quiz.q: Meena's plait is 45 cm long. How much shorter is it than 1 m?
quiz.mistake: Makes a mistake taking away from 100, or adds instead

quiz.q: Riya has a 3 m rope. She cuts off 120 cm for a swing. How much rope is left?
quiz.mistake: Takes 3 away from 120 without changing metres to cm

quiz.q: Kabir runs 5 rounds of a 100 m track. How far does he run?
quiz.explain: 5 rounds of 100 m is 5 × 100 = 500 m.
steps: One round = 100 m. Kabir runs 5 rounds.

quiz.q: Arjun is 1 m 32 cm tall. His sister is 1 m 18 cm tall. How much taller is Arjun?
steps: 1 m 32 cm = 132 cm, 1 m 18 cm = 118 cm
quiz.mistake: Adds the heights or takes away wrongly

quiz.q: Aisha joins 4 garland pieces, each 60 cm long. What is the total length?
quiz.mistake: Writes 240 cm as 240 m, or adds 4 + 60

quiz.q: Joseph's desk is 1 m long. How many 25 cm long books fit end to end along it?
quiz.mistake: Takes away 25 from 100 instead of dividing

quiz.q: Harpreet walks 650 m to school and then 650 m back home. How far does she walk in all?
steps: To school = 650 m; back home = 650 m.

quiz.q: Meena has a 75 cm ribbon and a 50 cm ribbon. What is their total length?

teach.ask: Gappu has a 2 m string and a 50 cm string. Gappu says together they are 52. Is that right?
teach.praise: Thank you! Change 2 m to 200 cm first, then add: 250 cm, which is 2 m 50 cm!
teach.nudge: Are metres and centimetres the same unit? What should Gappu do first?

revise.summary: To add or subtract lengths, first make the units the same. If you get 100 cm or more, change 100 cm into 1 m.
focus: Add lengths and write the answer in m and cm
Find how much longer or shorter
Find what is left after cutting
remember: 125 cm = 1 m 25 cm
How much longer: subtract the shorter from the longer
traps: Don't take away without changing m to cm first
Don't write 125 cm as 125 m
Don't count only one way for a there-and-back walk

learn.hook: Is your classroom door taller than your dad? Metres and centimetres can tell!
points: We measure short lengths, like a pencil, in centimetres (cm).
We measure longer lengths, like a room or a rope, in metres (m).
1 metre = 100 centimetres.
To change metres to centimetres, multiply by 100: 3 m = 300 cm.
1 m 30 cm means 100 cm + 30 cm = 130 cm.

example.q: Riya is 1 m 30 cm tall. What is her height in centimetres?

learn.reallife: A tailor measures you in centimetres. A cloth shop sells cloth by the metre.

quiz.q: How many centimetres make 1 metre?
quiz.explain: 1 metre is the same as 100 centimetres.
steps: The metre is the bigger unit; the centimetre is the smaller one.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up metres with kilograms (1000) or with minutes (60)

quiz.q: Which unit is best to measure the length of a pencil?
quiz.explain: A pencil is short, so we use centimetres. Kilogram measures weight and litre measures liquid.
steps: A pencil is short, so use a small unit of length.
Centimetre is a small unit of length.
Kilogram is for weight and litre for liquid, so: Centimetre.
quiz.mistake: Picks a unit that does not measure length

quiz.q: How many centimetres are there in 3 m?
quiz.explain: Each metre is 100 cm. 3 × 100 = 300 cm.

quiz.q: Which rope is longer: one that is 1 m long or one that is 90 cm long?
quiz.explain: 1 m = 100 cm, and 100 cm is more than 90 cm.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 90 is bigger than 1 without changing the units

quiz.q: A cloth piece is 400 cm long. How many metres is that?
quiz.explain: 100 cm make 1 m, so 400 cm make 400 ÷ 100 = 4 m.

quiz.q: Kabir's ruler is 30 cm long. How many such rulers placed end to end make exactly 3 m?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to change 3 m into 300 cm

quiz.q: Riya is 1 m 30 cm tall. What is her height in centimetres?
quiz.mistake: Writes 1 and 30 side by side, or writes 1 m as 1000 cm

quiz.q: Which length is the longest?
quiz.explain: Change all to cm: 2 m = 200 cm, 199 cm, 250 cm, 1 m 90 cm = 190 cm. 250 cm is the longest.
quiz.mistake: Compares numbers without changing them to the same unit

teach.ask: Gappu measured a rope: 2 m. Kabir says it is 200 cm. Who is right?
teach.praise: Both are right! 1 m is 100 cm, so 2 m is 200 cm. Gappu is happy!
teach.nudge: How many centimetres are in one metre? Can two answers both be correct?

revise.summary: We measure short lengths like a pencil in centimetres and longer lengths like a room in metres. 1 metre = 100 centimetres.
focus: Choose cm or m for a length
Change m to cm and cm to m
Compare lengths after changing to the same unit
remember: 1 metre = 100 centimetres
m to cm: multiply by 100 (3 m = 300 cm)
traps: 1 m is not 1000 cm or 60 cm
Don't multiply or divide by 10 instead of 100
Don't compare numbers without changing them to the same unit

topics.title: Fractions of a metre and measuring small things

learn.hook: Half a metre, a quarter metre, three-quarters of a metre... in centimetres, they are 50, 25 and 75!
points: Half a metre = 50 cm. A quarter metre = 25 cm. Three-quarters of a metre = 75 cm.
Measure small objects with a scale: put one end at 0 and read the number at the other end.
After measuring, we can order things from shortest to longest.
About 1 cm long: a fingernail's width, a peanut, a small bead, a staple pin.

example.q: A ribbon is three-quarters of a metre long. How many cm is that?

learn.reallife: At a cloth shop, you can buy half a metre or a quarter metre of ribbon for a rakhi or a craft project.

quiz.q: How many centimetres are in a quarter metre?
Which is three-quarters of a metre?
Lengths: pencil 14 cm, eraser 4 cm, crayon 9 cm. Which list is shortest to longest?
steps: Lengths: eraser 4 cm, crayon 9 cm, pencil 14 cm.
Shortest to longest: eraser, crayon, pencil.

quiz.q: Which is about 1 cm long?
quiz.explain: A peanut is about 1 cm.
steps: 1 cm is very small, about the width of a fingertip.
A pen, a bag and a bat are much longer.
A peanut is about 1 cm long.

quiz.q: A scale shows one end of a leaf at 0 and the other end at 7. How long is the leaf?
quiz.explain: Starting at 0, the end mark gives the length: 7 cm.
steps: The leaf starts at the 0 mark.
When an object starts at 0, the end mark gives the length.
The end is at 7, so the leaf is 7 cm long.

quiz.q: Mira has half a metre of lace and needs 75 cm. How much more lace does she need?
quiz.explain: Half a metre = 50 cm. 75 − 50 = 25 cm.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to change half a metre into cm

quiz.q: Two quarter-metre strips are joined. How long is the joined strip?
quiz.explain: 25 + 25 = 50 cm, which is half a metre.

quiz.q: Which is longest: 3/4 m, 70 cm, half a metre?
quiz.explain: 3/4 m = 75 cm, more than 70 cm and 50 cm.
steps: Change all to cm. 3/4 m = 3 × 25 = 75 cm.
Half a metre = 50 cm; the other is 70 cm.
75 cm is the biggest, so 3/4 m is longest.
quiz.mistake: Does not change fractions of a metre into cm

teach.ask: Gappu wants a quarter metre of ribbon but the shopkeeper asks 'how many centimetres?' Help Gappu.
teach.praise: A quarter metre is 100 ÷ 4 = 25 cm. Thank you!
teach.nudge: How many cm are in a metre, and how do you find a quarter of it?

revise.summary: Half a metre is 50 cm, a quarter metre is 25 cm and three-quarters of a metre is 75 cm. Measure small objects with a scale by putting one end at 0.
focus: Change fractions of a metre into cm
Measure with a scale starting at 0
Order lengths from shortest to longest
remember: Put one end at 0 and read the number at the other end
About 1 cm: a fingernail's width, a peanut, a small bead, a staple pin
traps: Don't write 3 and 4 side by side for 3/4 m
Don't compare fractions of a metre with cm until you change them into cm
Don't add 1 for the starting mark

learn.hook: No ruler? No problem! Your hand and feet can help you guess lengths.
points: To estimate means to make a smart guess, close to the real answer.
Use body measures: a handspan is about 15 cm, a big step is about 50 cm for a child.
A door is about 2 m tall. A cricket pitch is about 20 m long. An eraser is about 4 cm long.
Check your guess by measuring. A good estimate is close to the real length.

example.q: Riya's handspan is about 15 cm. Her table is 6 handspans long. About how long is the table?

learn.reallife: Before buying a mat, you can step across the room to guess if it will fit.

games.title: Good estimate?
items: A classroom door is about 2 m tall.
That is a little taller than most grown-ups.
A pencil is about 2 m long.
A pencil is about 15 to 20 cm long.
An eraser is about 4 cm long.
It fits easily in your hand.
A school bus is about 50 cm long.
A bus is many metres long.
A cricket bat is closer to 1 m than to 1 cm.
A cricket bat is a bit less than 1 m long.
A grain of rice is about 1 m long.
It is only a few millimetres, much less than 1 cm.

quiz.q: What is the best estimate for the height of a classroom door?
quiz.explain: A door is a little taller than a grown-up, which is about 2 m.
steps: A door is a little taller than a grown-up.
A grown-up is a bit less than 2 m tall.
So about 2 m. (2 cm is too small; 20 m and 200 m are too big.)
quiz.mistake: Picks the right number with the wrong unit

quiz.q: What is the best estimate for the length of an eraser?
quiz.explain: An eraser fits in your palm, so it is only a few centimetres long.
steps: An eraser fits in your palm.
So it is only a few centimetres long.
About 4 cm is the best estimate.
quiz.mistake: Does not picture how big a metre is

quiz.q: Riya's handspan is about 15 cm. Her table is 6 handspans long. About how long is the table?
quiz.explain: 6 handspans of 15 cm each is 6 × 15 = 90 cm.
steps: One handspan ≈ 15 cm. The table is 6 handspans.

quiz.q: Arjun's step is about 50 cm long. About how many steps will he take to walk 5 m?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to change metres to centimetres

quiz.q: Which of these is closest to 1 m long?
quiz.explain: A cricket bat is a little less than 1 m long. The others are much smaller or much bigger.
steps: A matchbox and a rice grain are tiny; a school bus is many metres long.
A cricket bat is a little less than 1 m, so it is the closest.
quiz.mistake: Does not have a picture of 1 m in mind

quiz.q: Kabir guessed that his book was 40 cm long. He measured it and it was 32 cm. How far off was his guess?
quiz.explain: 40 - 32 = 8 cm. His guess was 8 cm too long.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two lengths instead of finding the difference

quiz.q: Which of these would you measure in metres?
quiz.explain: A cricket pitch is long, about 20 m. The others are small and are measured in cm or smaller.
steps: Metres are used for long things.
An ant, a coin and a pencil are small (cm or less).
A cricket pitch is about 20 m long, so measure it in metres.
Answer: Length of a cricket pitch
quiz.mistake: Thinks metres are used for small things

quiz.q: A cricket pitch is about 20 m long. Meena walks along it 3 times. About how far does she walk?
steps: One walk along the pitch ≈ 20 m. Meena walks 3 times.

teach.ask: Gappu has no ruler but wants to know how long the bench is. What can Gappu do?
teach.praise: Smart! Use handspans or steps to estimate, then check with a ruler later. Gappu tried it!
teach.nudge: What could Gappu use from Gappu's own body to guess the length?

revise.summary: To estimate means to make a smart guess close to the real answer. Use body measures and known lengths, then check by measuring.
focus: Choose the best estimate with the right unit
Estimate lengths using handspans and steps
Find how far off a guess was
remember: Handspan about 15 cm; a child's big step about 50 cm
Door about 2 m tall; cricket pitch about 20 m long; eraser about 4 cm long
traps: Don't pick the right number with the wrong unit
Multiply, don't add: 6 handspans of 15 cm is 90 cm
Don't divide metres by a step length in cm; change m to cm first

topics.title: Ramps, treasure maps and broken scales

learn.hook: Your scale is broken and starts at 3! Can you still measure? Yes, with one clever subtraction.
points: To find how far a toy car rolls, measure from where it starts to where it stops, in cm.
On a map where each step is 1 cm, add the cm of each part of a route to find its length.
Compare routes to find the longest and shortest.
With a broken scale, length = end mark − start mark. From 3 to 11 is 11 − 3 = 8 cm.

example.q: A pencil is placed on a broken scale from the 4 cm mark to the 13 cm mark. How long is it?

learn.reallife: If your scale's zero is worn off, you can still measure by starting at 1 cm and taking away 1 from the reading!

quiz.q: A broken scale starts at 2 cm. A crayon goes from 2 to 10. How long is the crayon?
steps: The crayon starts at 2 and ends at 10 on the broken scale.

quiz.q: A toy car starts at the 15 cm mark and stops at the 62 cm mark on a tape. How far did it roll?
steps: Start = 15 cm mark; stop = 62 cm mark.

quiz.q: Car A rolls 48 cm down a ramp. Car B rolls 39 cm. How much further did car A go?
steps: Car A = 48 cm; Car B = 39 cm.

quiz.q: On a treasure map each step is 1 cm. Route 1: 4 cm + 3 cm + 2 cm. Route 2: 5 cm + 5 cm. Which is shorter?
quiz.explain: Route 1 = 9 cm, Route 2 = 10 cm. Route 1 is shorter.

quiz.q: How long is route 4 cm + 6 cm + 5 cm on the map?
A ribbon lies on a broken scale from 7 cm to 19 cm. How long is it?
steps: The ribbon goes from 7 cm to 19 cm.

quiz.q: Why can't you just read the end number on a broken scale?
options: The object does not start at 0
quiz.explain: The object starts at a mark that is not 0, so you must subtract the start.
steps: On a broken scale, the object does not start at 0.
The end number includes the part before the start.
So you must subtract the start mark from the end mark.
Answer: The object does not start at 0

quiz.q: A toy car rolls 25 cm from a low ramp and 40 cm from a high ramp. How much further from the high ramp?
steps: High ramp = 40 cm; low ramp = 25 cm.

teach.ask: Gappu's scale broke and now starts at 5. Gappu measured a stick from 5 to 17 and says 17 cm. Help Gappu.
teach.praise: 17 minus 5 is 12 cm! The stick did not start at 0.
teach.nudge: Where does the stick start, and what should you do with that number?

revise.summary: To find how far something rolls or how long it is, take the end mark minus the start mark. Add the cm of each part of a map route to find its length.
focus: Measure with a broken scale
Find distances rolled by toy cars
Add and compare route lengths on a map
remember: Length = end mark − start mark
From 3 to 11 is 11 − 3 = 8 cm
traps: Don't read only the end mark
Don't add the two marks
Compare total lengths, not the number of parts

learn.hook: A rope is 2 m long. How many 20 cm pieces can you cut from it? Let's find out!
points: On a number line, 1 m 50 cm sits halfway between 1 m and 2 m.
Mark metres on a number line, and centimetres between them: 100 cm, 150 cm, 200 cm.
To find how many pieces fit, change to the same unit and divide: 2 m = 200 cm, 200 ÷ 20 = 10.
Equal lengths can be written in different ways: 3 m 5 cm = 305 cm, and 4 m = 400 cm.

example.q: How many 25 cm pieces can be cut from a 2 m ribbon?

learn.reallife: Well depths, saree lengths and rope lengths are written in m and cm. Shopkeepers change them to cm to cut pieces.

quiz.q: How many 20 cm pieces can be cut from a 2 m rope?
On a number line marked 0 m, 1 m, 2 m, where is 1 m 50 cm?
quiz.explain: 1 m 50 cm is 50 cm more than 1 m and 50 cm less than 2 m.
steps: 1 m = 100 cm and 2 m = 200 cm; 150 is 50 more than 100 and 50 less than 200.
So it is halfway between 1 m and 2 m.
Answer: Halfway between 1 m and 2 m

quiz.q: Three wells are 305 cm, 3 m 50 cm and 3 m 5 cm deep. Which two are equally deep?
steps: Change all to cm: 305 cm; 3 m 50 cm = 350 cm; 3 m 5 cm = 300 + 5 = 305 cm.
So 305 cm and 3 m 5 cm are equally deep.

quiz.q: Which is the same as 450 cm?
A number line goes 100 cm, 120 cm, 140 cm, ? What is the next mark?
quiz.explain: It goes up by 20 cm each time: 140 + 20 = 160.
steps: 100 → 120 → 140: it goes up by 20 cm each time.

quiz.q: How many 50 cm pieces can be cut from a 3 m cloth?
A well is 6 m 8 cm deep. How many cm is that?
quiz.mistake: Writes 6 and 8 side by side as 68

quiz.q: Rita cuts 15 cm pieces from a 90 cm ribbon. How many pieces?

teach.ask: Gappu has a 2 m rope and wants 20 cm pieces for a craft. How can Gappu find how many pieces?
teach.praise: 2 m is 200 cm, and 200 ÷ 20 = 10 pieces. Craft time!
teach.nudge: What unit should both lengths be in, and then what do you do?

revise.summary: Metres and centimetres can be shown on a number line, and the same length can be written in different ways. To find how many pieces fit, change to the same unit and divide.
focus: Place m and cm on a number line
Change between m and cm, like 3 m 5 cm = 305 cm
Find how many pieces can be cut
remember: 1 m 50 cm is halfway between 1 m and 2 m
3 m 5 cm = 305 cm
traps: 3 m 5 cm is not 350 cm
Don't divide 2 by 20; change 2 m to 200 cm first
6 m 8 cm is 608 cm, not 68

learn.hook: Stand against the wall, put a book flat on your head and mark it. How tall are you?
points: Measure height from the floor to the top of the head, standing straight against a wall.
Record each child's height in a table, in cm or in m and cm.
The tallest child has the biggest height; the shortest has the smallest.
1 m = 100 cm. Children taller than 1 m have heights more than 100 cm.

example.q: Heights: Anu 128 cm, Bilal 1 m 35 cm, Chinku 98 cm. Who is the tallest? Who is shorter than 1 m?
example.answer: Bilal is tallest; Chinku is shorter than 1 m

learn.reallife: Doctors measure children's height at check-ups to see how much they have grown.

quiz.q: Heights: Rina 132 cm, Sonu 1 m 25 cm, Tia 1 m 40 cm. Who is the tallest?
quiz.explain: Tia: 140 cm is the biggest.
steps: Change all to cm: Rina 132 cm; Sonu 1 m 25 cm = 125 cm; Tia 1 m 40 cm = 140 cm.

quiz.q: In that group, how much taller is Tia than Sonu?
steps: Tia = 1 m 40 cm = 140 cm; Sonu = 1 m 25 cm = 125 cm.

quiz.q: A class records: 95 cm, 104 cm, 99 cm, 112 cm, 101 cm. How many children are taller than 1 m?
quiz.explain: Taller than 100 cm: 104, 112, 101. That is 3.
steps: 1 m = 100 cm. Taller than 1 m means more than 100 cm.
95 and 99 are less; 104, 112 and 101 are more.
So 3 children are taller than 1 m.

quiz.q: How should you stand to measure your height correctly?
options: Stand straight against a wall with feet flat
quiz.explain: Standing straight with heels on the floor gives the true height.
steps: To measure the true height, nothing should add or take away height.
Tall shoes add height; bending your knees takes it away.
So stand straight against a wall with feet flat.
Answer: Stand straight against a wall with feet flat
quiz.mistake: Does not think about fair measuring

quiz.q: Asha is 1 m 18 cm tall. What is her height in cm?
Heights: 120 cm, 97 cm, 108 cm. Who is the shortest?
quiz.explain: 97 is the smallest number.
steps: The heights are 120 cm, 97 cm and 108 cm.
The shortest is the smallest number: 97.
So the one at 97 cm is the shortest.

quiz.q: Ravi was 110 cm tall last year. Now he is 1 m 17 cm. How much did he grow?
steps: Now: 1 m 17 cm = 100 + 17 = 117 cm. Last year: 110 cm.

quiz.q: Heights: 98 cm, 1 m 2 cm, 99 cm, 1 m 10 cm. How many are shorter than 1 m?
quiz.explain: 98 cm and 99 cm are shorter than 100 cm.
steps: Shorter than 100 cm: 98 cm and 99 cm.

teach.ask: Gappu's class wants to find the tallest child. Explain how to measure and compare heights.
teach.praise: Measure straight against the wall, write it in a table, and the biggest number is the tallest!
teach.nudge: How do you measure fairly, and how do you find the tallest?

revise.summary: Measure height from the floor to the top of the head, standing straight against a wall. Record heights in a table and compare: children taller than 1 m are more than 100 cm.
focus: Find the tallest and shortest from a table
Change heights in m and cm into cm
Count heights more or less than 1 m
remember: 1 m 18 cm = 118 cm
Stand straight against a wall with feet flat
traps: Don't compare only the cm part without the metres
99 cm is not taller than 1 m
1 m 18 cm is not 1018 cm

topics.title: Perimeter: the boundary around a shape

learn.hook: A farmer wants to put a fence around his field. How much fencing wire does he need?
points: Perimeter is the total length of the boundary around a shape.
To find it, add the lengths of all the sides.
If a garden's edge is lined with bricks, count the bricks along the boundary to find its length in bricks.
A rectangle 5 m long and 3 m wide has perimeter 5 + 3 + 5 + 3 = 16 m.
You can estimate, then measure, the perimeter of real things like a book, a table or a lid.

example.q: A table top is 120 cm long and 60 cm wide. What is its perimeter?

learn.reallife: Lace stitched around a handkerchief, a fence around a field and a boundary wall around a school all show perimeter.

games.title: Perimeter facts
items: Perimeter is the length around the outside of a shape.
It is the total boundary length.
To find perimeter, multiply length by width.
A square with side 5 cm has perimeter 20 cm.
Lace around a handkerchief measures its perimeter.
The lace goes along the boundary.
It is a length, so cm or m.

quiz.q: A rectangle is 7 cm long and 4 cm wide. What is its perimeter?
A square garden has sides of 9 m. How much fencing goes around it?
steps: A square has 4 equal sides of 9 m.

quiz.q: A garden is lined with bricks: 10 bricks on each long side and 6 on each short side. How many bricks in all on the boundary? (No brick is shared at the corners.)
steps: Boundary = long side + short side + long side + short side.

quiz.q: What is perimeter?
options: The total length around a shape
quiz.explain: Perimeter is the length of the boundary.
steps: Perimeter is the boundary around a shape.
It is found by adding the lengths of all the sides.
So perimeter is the total length around a shape (not the space inside).
Answer: The total length around a shape

quiz.q: A triangle has sides 6 cm, 8 cm and 10 cm. What is its perimeter?
steps: Perimeter of a triangle = sum of its 3 sides.

quiz.q: Gopal guessed his book's perimeter is 100 cm. He measured sides of 25 cm and 20 cm. What is the true perimeter?
quiz.explain: 25 + 20 + 25 + 20 = 90 cm. His guess was 10 cm too much.
steps: A book is a rectangle: sides 25, 20, 25, 20 cm.
= 90 cm. (His guess, 100 cm, was 10 cm too much.)

quiz.q: Lace is put around a square handkerchief of side 30 cm. How much lace is needed?
steps: A square handkerchief has 4 equal sides of 30 cm.

quiz.q: A rectangular field is 50 m long and 30 m wide. Mohan walks once around it. How far does he walk?

teach.ask: Gappu wants to put ribbon around a photo frame. How can Gappu find how much ribbon is needed?
teach.praise: Measure each side and add them all. That is the perimeter!
teach.nudge: Which sides do you measure, and what do you do with the numbers?

revise.summary: Perimeter is the total length of the boundary around a shape. To find it, add the lengths of all the sides.
focus: Find the perimeter of rectangles, squares and triangles
Count bricks along a boundary
Solve fence and lace problems
remember: Perimeter = add the lengths of all the sides
Rectangle 5 m by 3 m: 5 + 3 + 5 + 3 = 16 m
Square of side 9 m: 4 × 9 = 36 m
traps: Don't add only two sides
Don't multiply the side by itself for a square's perimeter
Perimeter is not area

topics.title: Comparing boundaries: same perimeter, different shapes

learn.hook: A 4 by 2 rectangle and a 3 by 3 square look different. Yet their boundaries are exactly the same length!
points: On a dot grid, count the units along the boundary to compare shapes.
Different shapes can have the same perimeter: a 4 by 2 rectangle and a 3 by 3 square both have perimeter 12 units.
To find the shape with the smallest boundary, find each perimeter and compare.
To draw shapes with perimeter 20 cm, the length and width must add to 10: 5 by 5, 6 by 4, 7 by 3, 8 by 2, 9 by 1.

example.q: Draw two different rectangles with perimeter 20 cm.
steps: Length + width must be half of 20, which is 10.
example.answer: 6 cm by 4 cm, and 8 cm by 2 cm

learn.reallife: Two gardens can need the same length of fence even if one is long and thin and the other is square.

quiz.q: What is the perimeter of a 4 by 2 rectangle on a dot grid?
steps: A 4 by 2 rectangle has sides 4, 2, 4, 2 units.

quiz.q: Which has the same perimeter as a 3 by 3 square?
steps: Only the 4 by 2 rectangle has perimeter 12.
quiz.mistake: Thinks only identical shapes have the same perimeter

quiz.q: Garden A: 6 m by 2 m. Garden B: 4 m by 4 m. Garden C: 5 m by 2 m. Which has the smallest boundary?
quiz.explain: A: 16 m. B: 16 m. C: 14 m. C is smallest.

quiz.q: A rectangle has perimeter 20 cm and length 7 cm. What is its width?
quiz.explain: Length + width = 10. 10 − 7 = 3 cm.

quiz.q: Which rectangle does NOT have a perimeter of 20 cm?
steps: Perimeter of a rectangle = length + breadth + length + breadth.

quiz.q: Two shapes on a dot grid: an L-shape with perimeter 14 units and a rectangle 5 by 2. Which has the longer boundary?
quiz.explain: 5 + 2 + 5 + 2 = 14. Both are 14 units.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a different shape must have a different perimeter

quiz.q: A square has perimeter 20 cm. How long is each side?
quiz.explain: 4 equal sides: 20 ÷ 4 = 5 cm.

quiz.q: How many different rectangles with whole-cm sides have perimeter 12 cm? (Count 2 by 4 and 4 by 2 as the same.)
quiz.explain: Length + width = 6: 5 by 1, 4 by 2, 3 by 3. That is 3.

teach.ask: Gappu thinks a long thin rectangle always has a bigger boundary than a square. Show Gappu an example.
teach.praise: A 3 by 3 square and a 4 by 2 rectangle both have 12! Shapes can look different and still have the same boundary.
teach.nudge: Can you find a square and a rectangle with the same perimeter?

revise.summary: Different shapes can have the same perimeter, like a 4 by 2 rectangle and a 3 by 3 square. For a rectangle with perimeter 20 cm, the length and width must add to 10.
focus: Find and compare perimeters on a dot grid
Find a missing side from the perimeter
Draw different rectangles with the same perimeter
remember: 4 by 2 rectangle and 3 by 3 square: both 12 units
Perimeter 20 cm: length + width = 10 (5 by 5, 6 by 4, 7 by 3, 8 by 2, 9 by 1)
Square with perimeter 20 cm: 20 ÷ 4 = 5 cm
traps: Don't multiply length × width for perimeter
Don't think different shapes must have different perimeters
Don't take the length from 20: length + width = 10, so a 7 cm length gives a 3 cm width

topics.title: Trip to Mawlynnong: reading the details

learn.hook: Mawlynnong in Meghalaya is called one of the cleanest villages in Asia. Let's plan a school trip there!
points: A trip notice gives dates, times and costs. Read every detail carefully.
Use the costs in simple sums: cost for 3 children = 3 × cost for one.
To find how long a trip lasts, count the hours from the start time to the end time.
From 7 am to 12 noon is 5 hours; from 12 noon to 6 pm is 6 more hours. 5 + 6 = 11 hours.

example.q: The bus leaves at 7:00 am and returns at 6:00 pm. How long is the trip?

learn.reallife: Before any family trip, parents check the train time, ticket price and how long the journey takes.

items.text: Notice: trip on 14 March, bus 7:00 am to 6:00 pm, ₹250 per child, ₹400 per teacher. The trip is in the month of ___.
Notice: trip on 14 March, bus 7:00 am to 6:00 pm, ₹250 per child, ₹400 per teacher. The bus leaves at ___.
Notice: trip on 14 March, bus 7:00 am to 6:00 pm, ₹250 per child, ₹400 per teacher. One child pays ₹___.
Notice: trip on 14 March, bus 7:00 am to 6:00 pm, ₹250 per child, ₹400 per teacher. The trip lasts ___ hours.

quiz.q: Trip notice: School trip to Mawlynnong on 14 March. Bus leaves at 7:00 am, returns at 6:00 pm. Cost: ₹250 per child, ₹400 per teacher. How much do 3 children pay?
steps: Cost for one child = ₹250. 3 children go.

quiz.q: Trip notice: School trip to Mawlynnong on 14 March. Bus leaves at 7:00 am, returns at 6:00 pm. Cost: ₹250 per child, ₹400 per teacher. How long is the trip from leaving to returning?
quiz.explain: 7 am to 12 noon is 5 hours, then to 6 pm is 6 more: 11 hours.

quiz.q: Trip notice: School trip to Mawlynnong on 14 March. Bus leaves at 7:00 am, returns at 6:00 pm. Cost: ₹250 per child, ₹400 per teacher. How much more does a teacher pay than a child?
Trip notice: School trip to Mawlynnong on 14 March. Bus leaves at 7:00 am, returns at 6:00 pm. Cost: ₹250 per child, ₹400 per teacher. What is the cost for 1 teacher and 2 children?
A bus leaves at 8 am and reaches at 1 pm. How many hours is the journey?
quiz.explain: 8 am to 12 noon is 4 hours, then 1 more hour to 1 pm: 5 hours.

quiz.q: The trip bus returns at 6:00 pm. Lunch is from 1:00 pm to 2:00 pm. How many hours of the trip are left after lunch?
quiz.explain: From 2 pm to 6 pm is 4 hours.
steps: Lunch ends at 2:00 pm. The bus returns at 6:00 pm.
Count the hours from 2 pm to 6 pm: 3, 4, 5, 6.

quiz.q: Trip notice: School trip to Mawlynnong on 14 March. Bus leaves at 7:00 am, returns at 6:00 pm. Cost: ₹250 per child, ₹400 per teacher. On which date is the trip?
quiz.explain: The notice says 14 March.
steps: Read the notice for the date.
It says: School trip to Mawlynnong on 14 March.
7, 6 and 250 are times or costs, not the date.
quiz.mistake: Reads a time as a date

quiz.q: A trip costs ₹250 per child. 10 children go. What is the total cost?
steps: Cost for one child = ₹250. 10 children go.

teach.ask: Gappu wants to join the school trip. Explain how to read the notice to find the cost and the time.
teach.praise: ₹250 for me, and the trip is 11 hours long. I'm ready for Mawlynnong!
teach.nudge: What details does the notice give, and how do you find the trip length?

revise.summary: A trip notice gives dates, times and costs, so read every detail carefully. Use the costs in simple sums and count the hours from the start time to the end time.
focus: Read dates, times and costs from a notice
Find costs for several people
Find how many hours a trip or journey lasts
remember: Cost for 3 children = 3 × cost for one
7 am to 12 noon is 5 hours; 12 noon to 6 pm is 6 more. 5 + 6 = 11 hours
traps: Don't subtract 6 from 7 for 7 am to 6 pm; count through 12 noon
Don't add 3 to 250; multiply
Don't read a time as a date

learn.hook: Oranges cost ₹60 per kg. How much for 2 kg? For 3 kg? Let's go shopping!
points: A price list 'per kg' tells the cost of 1 kg.
For 2 kg, double the cost of 1 kg: 2 × ₹60 = ₹120.
For 3 kg, add the cost three times or multiply: ₹60 + ₹60 + ₹60 = 3 × ₹60 = ₹180.
Doubling trick: double ₹45 = ₹40 + ₹40 + ₹5 + ₹5 = ₹90.

example.q: Ginger costs ₹120 per kg. How much for 3 kg?

learn.reallife: At a sabzi mandi, prices are written per kg on little boards. Shoppers quickly double or triple them in their heads.

quiz.q: Market price list (per kg): oranges ₹60, pineapple ₹45, ginger ₹120, tomatoes ₹38, potatoes ₹25. How much do 2 kg of oranges cost?
quiz.explain: Double ₹60 = ₹120.

quiz.q: Market price list (per kg): oranges ₹60, pineapple ₹45, ginger ₹120, tomatoes ₹38, potatoes ₹25. How much do 2 kg of pineapple cost?
Market price list (per kg): oranges ₹60, pineapple ₹45, ginger ₹120, tomatoes ₹38, potatoes ₹25. How much do 3 kg of potatoes cost?
Market price list (per kg): oranges ₹60, pineapple ₹45, ginger ₹120, tomatoes ₹38, potatoes ₹25. How much do 3 kg of ginger cost?
Market price list (per kg): oranges ₹60, pineapple ₹45, ginger ₹120, tomatoes ₹38, potatoes ₹25. How much do 2 kg of tomatoes cost?
What does '₹45 per kg' mean?
quiz.explain: 'Per kg' means for each kilogram.
steps: So ₹45 per kg means each 1 kg costs ₹45.
It is not the price of 1 fruit or 1 g.

quiz.q: Which is the same as the cost of 3 kg of oranges at ₹60 per kg?
quiz.explain: 3 kg means ₹60 three times.
steps: 3 kg at ₹60 per kg means ₹60 for each kilogram.

quiz.q: Lam buys 2 kg of ginger at ₹120 per kg and 1 kg of potatoes at ₹25. How much does he pay?

teach.ask: Gappu sees 'Pineapple ₹45 per kg' and wants 2 kg. How should Gappu work out the cost?
teach.praise: Double ₹45 is ₹90! Per kg means for each kilogram.
teach.nudge: What does 'per kg' mean, and what do you do for 2 kg?

revise.summary: A price 'per kg' tells the cost of 1 kg. For 2 kg, double it; for 3 kg, add it three times or multiply by 3.
focus: Find the cost of 2 kg and 3 kg from a price list
Double numbers using the doubling trick
Find the total cost of mixed items
remember: 'Per kg' means for each kilogram
traps: Don't add 2 to the price; double it
Don't double when 3 kg is asked
Don't double only the tens

topics.title: Shop bills: totals and exact amounts

learn.hook: Iba has exactly ₹163. Which items can she buy to spend every rupee?
points: To find a bill total, add the prices of all items.
To spend an exact amount, try combinations of prices that add up to it.
If a number in a bill is missing, find it by counting on: total − known prices.
A number line or play money helps: start at the known amount and jump to the total.

example.q: Prices: oranges ₹60, pineapple ₹45, tomatoes ₹38, sugar ₹20. Which four items together cost exactly ₹163?

learn.reallife: When you shop with a fixed amount of pocket money, you check different combinations to spend it well.

quiz.q: A bill has: rice ₹65, dal ₹48, oil ₹110. What is the total?
Prices: oranges ₹60, ginger ₹120, potatoes ₹25, tomatoes ₹38. Which items cost exactly ₹145?
steps: Add each pair: ginger + tomatoes = 120 + 38 = 158; oranges + potatoes = 60 + 25 = 85.

quiz.q: Prices: oranges ₹60, pineapple ₹45, tomatoes ₹38, sugar ₹20. Which combination costs exactly ₹163?
A bill says: soap ₹35, toothpaste ₹___, total ₹120. What is the missing price?
steps: Total = soap + toothpaste, so toothpaste = total − soap.
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of finding the missing part

quiz.q: A bill: biscuits ₹30, milk ₹54, bread ₹___. Total ₹124. What does the bread cost?
Iba has ₹100. Can she buy pineapple (₹45) and tomatoes (₹38) together?
quiz.explain: 45 + 38 = 83, which is less than ₹100.
steps: ₹83 is less than ₹100, so Yes, she can buy them.

quiz.q: Which pair costs exactly ₹100? Prices: ₹62, ₹38, ₹45, ₹65
A shop bill: 2 kg potatoes at ₹25 per kg and 1 kg onions at ₹40. What is the total?

teach.ask: Gappu has exactly ₹100 and wants to spend all of it on two items. How should Gappu choose?
teach.praise: I tried pairs until two prices added to exactly ₹100. ₹62 + ₹38!
teach.nudge: How do you test whether two prices make exactly ₹100?

revise.summary: To find a bill total, add the prices of all items. To find a missing price, take the known prices away from the total, or count on.
focus: Add a bill total
Find items that cost an exact amount
Find a missing price in a bill
remember: Missing price = total − known prices
Count on: start at the known amount and jump to the total
traps: Don't forget to carry
Don't add instead of finding the missing part
Don't forget one item or the 2 kg

learn.hook: You pay ₹200 for things costing ₹163. The shopkeeper hands back money. How much?
points: Choose notes and coins that cover the cost. Check: is the money enough?
Balance (change) = money paid − cost.
The same purchase gives different change for different amounts paid: with ₹500 the change is 500 − 163 = ₹337.
Count on to check change: 163 + 7 = 170, 170 + 30 = 200. Change = 37.

example.q: A bill is ₹145. Lou pays with a ₹500 note. What balance does he get?

learn.reallife: At a sweet shop, the shopkeeper says the change aloud as he counts it back. You can check it the same way!

games.title: Enough money?
items: ₹200 is enough for a bill of ₹185.
Two ₹50 notes are enough for a bill of ₹120.
Paying ₹500 for a ₹163 bill gives ₹337 change.
If you pay the exact amount, the change is ₹0.

quiz.q: Cost ₹163. Paid ₹200. What is the balance?
For the same ₹163 bill, what is the balance if ₹500 is paid?
Daisy's bill is ₹240. She has one ₹100 note and two ₹50 notes. Is it enough?
steps: Add the value of the notes: ₹100 + ₹50 + ₹50.
₹200 is less than ₹240, so No, it is not enough.
quiz.mistake: Counts notes instead of their value

quiz.q: A toy costs ₹85. Raju pays ₹100. What change should he get?
Which notes are enough to pay ₹275 with the fewest notes?
quiz.explain: ₹200 + ₹100 = ₹300, enough for ₹275. The others are less than ₹275.
quiz.mistake: Picks an amount less than the cost

quiz.q: A bill is ₹348. Meera pays ₹400. How much balance does she get?
Sam got ₹15 change after paying ₹100. What was his bill?
quiz.explain: Bill = paid − change = 100 − 15 = 85.
steps: Paid = bill + change, so bill = paid − change.
quiz.mistake: Adds the change to the money paid

quiz.q: Two children buy the same ₹120 snack box. Anil pays ₹200, Bina pays ₹150. How much more change does Anil get?

teach.ask: Gappu buys sweets for ₹163 and pays ₹200. How can Gappu check the change is right?
teach.praise: 200 − 163 = 37, and 163 + 37 = 200. My change is right!
teach.nudge: How do you find change, and how can you check it?

revise.summary: Choose notes and coins that cover the cost, then find the balance: money paid − cost. Count on to check the change.
focus: Find the balance (change)
Check if the money is enough
Find the bill from the money paid and the change
remember: Balance (change) = money paid − cost
Count on to check: 163 + 7 = 170, 170 + 30 = 200
traps: Count the value of notes, not the number of notes
Don't forget to borrow, especially across zeros
Bill = paid − change; don't add the change

learn.hook: Put 1 to 6 on a triangle so that every side adds to the same number. Can you make it 9? 12? 13?
points: A magic triangle has 3 corner circles and 3 middle circles. Each side has 2 corners and 1 middle.
Place 1 to 6 once each so each side adds to the same total.
Corners are counted on two sides. Small numbers at the corners give the smallest total (9). Big numbers at the corners give the biggest total (12).
Possible side totals are only 9, 10, 11 and 12.
13 is impossible: even with the biggest corners (4, 5, 6), the sides can only reach 12.

example.q: Make each side add to 9.
steps: Put the smallest numbers 1, 2, 3 at the corners.

learn.reallife: Puzzles like magic triangles and magic squares have been enjoyed in India for hundreds of years, even carved in temples!

games.title: Magic triangle facts
items: Big numbers at the corners give a big side total.

quiz.q: To make the biggest side total, which numbers go at the corners?

points: Estimate a difference first by rounding: 586 − 412 is about 600 − 400 = 200.

learn.hook: The village had 4500 trees. 1250 were planted this year. How many are old? Subtraction to the rescue!
points: Write the bigger number on top. Line up ones, tens, hundreds and thousands.

With zeros, like 6000 - 2475, borrow across: 6000 becomes 5 thousands, 9 hundreds, 9 tens and 10 ones.

example.q: Subtract 7302 - 4568.

games.title: Check by adding
items: Adding back gives the starting number, so it is correct.
In 7302 - 4568, we must borrow in the ones place.
2 is less than 8, so we borrow.
When we borrow, the top digit gets 100 more.
It gets 10 more, because 1 from the next place is 10 here.

quiz.explain: No borrowing is needed: 8 - 5 = 3, 7 - 4 = 3, 6 - 3 = 3, 5 - 2 = 3.
Borrow across the zeros: 6000 is 5 thousands, 9 hundreds, 9 tens and 10 ones. 10 - 5 = 5, 9 - 7 = 2, 9 - 4 = 5, 5 - 2 = 3. So 3525.

Find a missing number and check by adding

learn.hook: A good problem-solver first asks: should I add or subtract? Let's learn the clue words!
points: Read the problem twice. Find what is given and what is asked.
Words like 'altogether', 'in all' and 'total' usually mean add.
Words like 'how many more', 'how many left' and 'difference' usually mean subtract.
Some problems have two steps. Do one step at a time.
Check if your answer makes sense.

topics.title: Estimating and using a pan balance

learn.hook: Is your water bottle less than 1 kg, about 1 kg or more than 1 kg? Guess, then check on a balance!
points: Estimate: hold a 1 kg packet in one hand and an object in the other. Is it lighter, about the same, or heavier?

topics.title: Market survey: by weight or by volume?

learn.hook: In a shop, rice is sold in kg but oil is sold in litres. Why the difference?
points: Solids like rice, dal, sugar, vegetables and fruit are sold by weight (g or kg).
Liquids like milk, oil, juice and water are sold by volume (ml or L).
Common weight packs: 100 g, 200 g, 250 g, 500 g, 1 kg, 5 kg.
Common liquid packs: 200 ml, 500 ml, 1 L, 2 L, 5 L.
Read the label: it tells how much is inside the pack.

example.q: Which unit is printed on a milk packet and which on a sugar packet?
steps: Milk is a liquid: sold by volume, so ml or L.
Sugar is a solid: sold by weight, so g or kg.
example.answer: Milk in ml or L; sugar in g or kg

learn.reallife: Go with your family to a kirana shop and read the labels: '500 g biscuits', '1 L oil', '200 ml juice'!

games.title: Sold by weight or by volume?
