topics.title: How much water do we use?

learn.hook: A bucket bath, a glass of water, watering plants... Every activity uses water. Which uses the most?
points: A child drinks about 1 to 2 litres of water a day. A cow drinks about 50 litres or more.
A bucket bath uses about 15 to 20 litres. A shower can use much more.
Washing clothes, cleaning floors and watering plants use many litres too.
To compare activities, put the estimated litres in a table and find the most and the least.

example.q: Estimates: bath 20 L, brushing teeth 2 L, washing clothes 40 L, drinking 2 L. Which uses the most and which the least?
steps: Least: brushing teeth and drinking, 2 L each.
example.answer: Most: washing clothes; least: brushing and drinking

learn.reallife: Many villages and cities face water shortage in summer. Knowing how much we use helps us save it.

quiz.q: About how much water does a child drink in a day?
quiz.explain: A child drinks around 6 to 8 glasses, about 1 to 2 litres.
steps: A child drinks about 6 to 8 glasses of water a day.
10 ml is too little; 50 L and 100 L are far too much.
quiz.mistake: Picks a very big or very small amount

quiz.q: Which uses the most water?
quiz.explain: Washing clothes needs many buckets of water.
steps: Drinking, brushing with a mug and washing your face use a little water.
Washing clothes by hand needs many buckets.
So washing clothes uses the most.
quiz.mistake: Does not think about the amount used

quiz.q: Estimates: bath 20 L, cooking 10 L, cleaning 15 L, drinking 8 L for a family. Which uses the least?
quiz.explain: 8 L is the smallest.
steps: Bath 20 L, cooking 10 L, cleaning 15 L, drinking 8 L.

quiz.q: In that table, how much more water is used for the bath than for cooking?
A family of 4 each takes a 20 L bucket bath daily. How much water for baths in a day?
Which is a sensible amount for a cow to drink in a day?
quiz.explain: A cow is big and drinks many litres, about 50 L or more.
steps: A cow is a big animal and drinks many litres a day.
5 ml and 50 ml are tiny; 5000 L is far too much.
quiz.mistake: Uses ml for a large amount

quiz.q: Mohan waters plants with a 10 L bucket, 3 times. How much water does he use?
steps: One bucket = 10 L. He uses it 3 times.

quiz.q: A family drinks 8 L, cooks with 12 L and washes dishes with 25 L. What is the total?

teach.nudge: How can you measure or estimate each activity and compare them?

revise.summary: We use water for drinking, baths, washing and cleaning. Put estimated litres in a table to compare activities and find the most and the least.

Find the most and least from a table
Add and multiply litres used

A bucket bath uses about 15 to 20 litres

learn.hook: Drip, drip, drip... A leaking tap can waste a whole bucket of water every day!
points: Put a mug under a leaking tap for one hour and measure the water collected.
Daily loss = loss in 1 hour × 24 hours. Weekly loss = daily loss × 7.
If a tap leaks 500 ml in an hour, it wastes 24 × 500 = 12,000 ml = 12 L a day, and 84 L a week.
Ways to save water: fix leaks, close the tap while brushing, use a bucket not a shower, reuse water from washing vegetables for plants.

example.q: A tap leaks 250 ml in one hour. How much does it waste in one day (24 hours)?

learn.reallife: Some schools hold 'Save Water' drives where children check every tap and report leaks.

games.title: Saves water or wastes water?
items: Using a bucket for a bath
Washing a car with a running hose

quiz.q: A tap leaks 500 ml in 1 hour. How much does it leak in 24 hours?
A tap wastes 12 L a day. How much does it waste in a week?
steps: A week has 7 days; 12 L wasted each day.

quiz.q: A tap fills a 100 ml cup in 1 hour from drips. How many ml in 10 hours?
Which is the best way to save water?
options: Turn off the tap while brushing
Let the tap run while soaping hands
Wash the car with a running hose
quiz.explain: Turning the tap off when not in use saves many litres.
steps: Water is saved when the tap is not running for nothing.
Leaving leaks, running taps and hoses all waste water.
So turn off the tap while brushing.
Answer: Turn off the tap while brushing
quiz.mistake: Does not see which habit wastes water

quiz.q: A tap leaks 200 ml an hour. How much does it leak in 5 hours?
Two taps leak 6 L and 4 L each day. How much water is wasted in a day?
steps: Water wasted in a day = both taps added.

quiz.q: How many hours are there in a day, for working out daily water loss?
quiz.explain: A day has 24 hours.
steps: One day is from midnight to midnight.
(12 hours is only half a day.)

quiz.q: Water from washing vegetables can be...
quiz.explain: Reusing water for plants saves fresh water.

quiz.mistake: Does not think of reusing water

teach.ask: Gappu's tap is dripping. Gappu says it is only a little water. How would you show how much is wasted?
teach.praise: One hour times 24 is a lot in a day, and even more in a week! I will get it fixed.
teach.nudge: How can you measure the leak, and how do you find the loss for a day?

revise.summary: Measure the water a leaking tap wastes in one hour, then multiply by 24 for a day and by 7 for a week. We can save water by fixing leaks and closing taps.
focus: Find daily and weekly water loss from a leak
Change ml into L
Know ways to save water
remember: Daily loss = loss in 1 hour × 24. Weekly loss = daily loss × 7
500 ml an hour: 24 × 500 = 12,000 ml = 12 L a day, 84 L a week
Save water: fix leaks, close the tap while brushing, use a bucket, reuse water
traps: Don't forget to multiply by 24
A day has 24 hours, not 12
Multiply, don't add: 7 × 12, not 7 + 12

learn.hook: A frog jumps 3 steps at a time on a number line: 3, 6, 9, 12... Will it ever land on 20?
points: Jumping in equal steps from 0 lands on multiples: jumps of 4 land on 4, 8, 12, 16, 20...
A number is reached by a jump if it is a multiple of the jump size: 20 is a multiple of 4 (4 × 5) but not of 3.
The number of jumps to reach a target is target ÷ jump size: 24 ÷ 6 = 4 jumps.
The smallest 3-digit number reached by jumps of 8 is 104 (8 × 13).
Bigger jumps reach a number in fewer jumps: to reach 24, a 3-jumper needs 8 jumps, an 8-jumper needs only 3.

example.q: A rabbit jumps 4 at a time from 0. How many jumps to reach 36?

learn.reallife: Skipping steps on a staircase two or three at a time, you land only on certain steps: the multiples!

quiz.q: A frog jumps 3 at a time from 0. Which number will it land on?
quiz.explain: 21 = 3 × 7, so it is a multiple of 3.
steps: A 3-jumper lands on the multiples of 3: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 24 ...
21 = 3 × 7, so it is on the list.
quiz.mistake: Picks a number close to a multiple

quiz.q: A deer jumps 6 at a time. How many jumps to reach 48?
quiz.explain: 48 ÷ 6 = 8 jumps.
steps: Each jump is 6. To reach 48, find how many 6s make 48.

quiz.q: A kangaroo jumps 8 at a time. Does it land on 60?
options: Yes, it lands on every number
No, 60 is not a multiple of 8
quiz.explain: 8 × 7 = 56 and 8 × 8 = 64. It jumps over 60.
steps: No, 60 is not a multiple of 8.
Answer: No, 60 is not a multiple of 8
quiz.mistake: Thinks every even number is a multiple of 8

steps: So the 4-jumper lands on 100. (96 has only 2 digits.)

quiz.mistake: Thinks all even numbers are multiples of 4

Find the number of jumps to reach a target
Find the smallest 3-digit multiple
remember: Jumps of 4 land on 4, 8, 12, 16, 20...

Smallest 3-digit number reached by jumps of 8: 104 (8 × 13)
traps: Every even number is not a multiple of 4 or 8
Don't pick 96 as a 3-digit number
Divide, don't subtract, to count the jumps

learn.hook: A 3-jumper and a 4-jumper start together at 0. Where do they first land on the same number?
points: A common multiple is a number that is a multiple of both jump sizes.
The first common landing point of 3 and 4 is 12. For 6 and 8 it is 24.
In a chase, two jumpers meet where their multiples match.
In a multiplication chart, colour the rows of two numbers to see their common multiples.

example.q: A cat jumps 6 at a time and a rat jumps 4 at a time, both from 0. Where do they first meet?

learn.reallife: If one bell rings every 3 minutes and another every 4 minutes, they ring together every 12 minutes!

quiz.q: What is the first common landing point of a 3-jumper and a 4-jumper?
steps: The first number in both lists is 12.

quiz.q: What is the first common landing point of a 6-jumper and an 8-jumper?
Which number is a common multiple of 2 and 5?
quiz.explain: 20 is in both tables: 2 × 10 and 5 × 4.

12 and 15 are in only one table; 25 is only in the 5s.

steps: But 18 is not in the 4s table (4 × 4 = 16, 4 × 5 = 20). So 18 is NOT common.

learn.hook: 4 plates with 6 laddoos on each. Count one by one? No way! Multiply!
points: Multiplication is a quick way to add equal groups.
An array is objects in rows and columns. 3 rows of 7 = 3 × 7 = 21.
Order does not change the answer: 6 × 4 = 4 × 6.
Any number × 1 = the same number. Any number × 0 = 0.

quiz.explain: 4 groups of 6 is 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 24. That is 4 × 6.
steps: 4 plates with 6 laddoos each: 4 equal groups of 6.

quiz.q: A rangoli has 3 rows of diyas with 7 diyas in each row. How many diyas are there?
quiz.explain: 3 rows of 7 is 3 × 7 = 21.
steps: 3 rows with 7 diyas each: 3 equal groups of 7.
quiz.mistake: Adds the rows and the diyas in a row

quiz.q: What is 8 × 7?
quiz.explain: 8 × 7 = 56. You can think 8 × 7 = 7 × 8.

quiz.q: Which is the same as 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 + 5?

revise.summary: Multiplication is a quick way to add equal groups. Order does not change the answer, any number × 1 is the same number and any number × 0 is 0.

Use the order, × 1 and × 0 rules
remember: Array: 3 rows of 7 = 3 × 7 = 21

Solve tray problems with × and ÷
Find different arrays for a number

points: Doubling means multiplying by 2: double 9 = 18.

The ones digit of a double depends only on the ones digit: double of a number ending in 7 ends in 4 (7 + 7 = 14).
Any doubled number is even, because it is made of two equal halves.

learn.hook: A multiplication chart is full of hidden patterns. Fold it along the diagonal and the two halves match!
points: In a multiplication chart, each box = row number × column number.
Order does not change the product: 3 × 4 = 4 × 3 = 12. So the chart is the same on both sides of the diagonal.
The diagonal from the top-left shows square numbers: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36...
Rows of even numbers (2, 4, 6...) have only even products.
Rows of odd numbers (3, 5, 7...) go odd, even, odd, even.

example.q: Which box of the chart has row 6 and column 7? What else has the same number?

learn.reallife: Multiplication charts hang in many classrooms. Spotting patterns makes the tables easier to remember!

games.title: Chart patterns

Every number in the 6s row is even.

topics.title: Odd and even sums, window frames and a grid puzzle

learn.hook: Odd + odd = even. Even + even = even. Odd + even = odd. Always! Can you use this to solve a puzzle?
points: Odd + odd = even (3 + 5 = 8). Even + even = even (4 + 6 = 10). Odd + even = odd (3 + 4 = 7).

example.q: A zoo elephant is given 125 kg of food each day. How much food does it get in 7 days?

learn.reallife: Zoo keepers plan how much food to buy for each animal for a week or a month.

quiz.q: Suppose an elephant drinks 150 litres of water a day. How much does it drink in 4 days?
A zoo elephant is given 125 kg of food each day. How much food is that in 7 days?
A tiger cub naps 15 hours a day. How many hours does it nap in 6 days?
Each safari jeep carries 6 visitors. 35 jeeps go out in a day. How many visitors go on safari?
What is 23 × 12?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies by 10 only and forgets the 2

quiz.q: A forest guard walks 14 km every day. How far does she walk in 12 days?
A ticket to the leopard safari costs ₹45. How much do 20 children pay altogether?
Which is the same as 16 × 25?
quiz.explain: 25 = 20 + 5, so 16 × 25 = 16 × 20 + 16 × 5. Each part must be multiplied by 16.
quiz.mistake: Splits 25 but forgets to multiply the 5 by 16

teach.ask: Gappu wants to find 23 × 12 but it looks too big! How can Gappu make it easier?
teach.praise: Wonderful! 23 × 10 = 230 and 23 × 2 = 46. Add them: 276. Gappu did it!
teach.nudge: Can Gappu split 12 into an easy 10 and a small part?

revise.summary: When the same amount repeats every day or for every animal, multiply. Break numbers into hundreds, tens and ones, or split a 2-digit multiplier.

Multiply by a 2-digit number by splitting it
Multiply by 20
remember: Multiplying by 20 is like multiplying by 2 and then by 10
traps: Don't add instead of multiplying
Don't multiply only by 10 and forget the 2
Don't multiply only one part by the number; multiply each part

learn.hook: Some forest puzzles need two steps. Plan first, then solve one step at a time!
points: Read the problem and find what is asked at the end.
Find the hidden first step. For example, find the cost of all the tickets before finding the change.
Do the steps in order and write each answer.
Check: does the final answer make sense?

example.q: A forest has 3 lakes with 45 ducks on each. 28 ducks fly away. How many ducks are left?

learn.reallife: A school trip to a national park needs two-step planning: total ticket cost, then change from the money collected.

games.title: Plan the steps
games.prompt: Put the steps in order: tickets cost ₹125 each. Find the change from ₹1000 for 6 tickets.

quiz.q: A viewing gallery has 4 rows of 25 seats. 63 seats are filled. How many seats are empty?
quiz.explain: Total seats: 4 × 25 = 100. Empty: 100 - 63 = 37.
quiz.mistake: Stops after finding the total seats

quiz.q: Safari tickets cost ₹30 for an adult and ₹15 for a child. How much do 2 adults and 3 children pay?
quiz.mistake: Uses the adult price for everyone or mixes up the numbers

quiz.q: 96 bananas are shared equally among 8 elephants. How many bananas does each elephant get?
A forest has 3 lakes with 45 ducks on each lake. 28 ducks fly away. How many ducks are left?
quiz.explain: 3 × 45 = 135 ducks. 135 - 28 = 107 ducks left.
quiz.mistake: Makes a borrowing mistake in the second step (gets 117)

quiz.q: A ranger buys 6 bags of seeds at ₹125 each. He pays with ₹1000. How much change does he get?
quiz.mistake: Gives the cost instead of the change

quiz.q: A wildlife park gets 1500 visitors each day it is open. It is closed on Mondays. How many visitors come in one week?
quiz.explain: The park is open 7 - 1 = 6 days. 6 × 1500 = 9000 visitors.

quiz.q: 240 saplings are planted in rows of 12. How many rows are there?
In a camp, 5 grown-up elephants eat 150 kg each and 2 baby elephants eat 50 kg each in a day. How much food do they eat in all?
quiz.explain: Grown-ups: 5 × 150 = 750 kg. Babies: 2 × 50 = 100 kg. Total: 850 kg.

teach.ask: Gappu wants to know the change from ₹1000 after buying 6 tickets of ₹125. Gappu is stuck. What first?
teach.praise: Super! First find the cost (6 × 125 = 750), then the change (1000 - 750 = 250). Two steps done!
teach.nudge: What must Gappu find before the change? How much do all the tickets cost?

revise.summary: Two-step problems have a hidden first step, like finding the cost of all the tickets before the change. Do the steps in order and check the final answer makes sense.
focus: Find the hidden first step
Solve two-step problems with ×, ÷, + and −
Check that the answer makes sense
remember: Find what is asked at the end first
traps: Don't stop after the first step
Don't give the cost when the change is asked
Don't count days the park is closed

learn.hook: Fold a butterfly picture down the middle. Both halves match perfectly! That fold is a line of symmetry.
points: A line of symmetry cuts a shape into two halves that match exactly when folded.
Some shapes have one line of symmetry, some have many, and some have none.
A square has 4 lines of symmetry. A rectangle that is not a square has 2.
A triangle with all sides equal has 3 lines of symmetry. A circle has endless lines of symmetry.
Letters like A, T and V have a standing (vertical) line of symmetry. B, C and E have a lying (horizontal) one. F, L, N and S have none.

example.q: How many lines of symmetry does the letter H have?
steps: Fold H from top to bottom down the middle: the halves match.
Fold H from left to right across the middle: the halves match.

learn.reallife: Rangoli, the Taj Mahal from the front, leaves and many logos are symmetrical.

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
quiz.explain: A square can be folded in half 4 ways: up-down, left-right and along both corner-to-corner lines.
steps: A line of symmetry is a fold where both halves match exactly.
A square folds evenly up-down, left-right, and along both corner-to-corner lines.

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle that is not a square have?
quiz.explain: It folds evenly only across the middle in two ways. A corner-to-corner fold does not make the halves match.
steps: Fold a rectangle across the middle and along the middle: both halves match.
Fold it corner to corner: the halves do not match.
So a rectangle (not a square) has 2 lines of symmetry.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the diagonals of a rectangle are lines of symmetry, like in a square

quiz.q: Which letter has a line of symmetry?
quiz.explain: A folds down the middle into two matching halves. F, L and N do not match when folded.
steps: Fold each letter down the middle and check if the halves match.
A: the left and right halves match.
F, L and N do not match when folded, so the answer is A.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any letter with straight lines is symmetrical

quiz.q: Which letter has NO line of symmetry?
quiz.explain: No fold makes the two halves of S match. H, T and E each have at least one line of symmetry.
steps: H, T and E each fold into matching halves (at least one way).
No fold makes the two halves of S match.
Looking the same upside down is a turn, not a fold. So S has no line of symmetry.
quiz.mistake: Thinks S is symmetrical because it looks the same when turned upside down

quiz.q: A triangle has all 3 sides equal. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
quiz.explain: You can fold it from each corner to the middle of the opposite side. That is 3 lines.
steps: Fold from each corner to the middle of the opposite side.
Each of these folds makes matching halves.
There are 3 corners, so 3 lines of symmetry.

quiz.q: Which letter has a lying (horizontal) line of symmetry, so its top half matches its bottom half?
quiz.explain: B folded from top to bottom matches. A, T and V have only a standing line of symmetry.
steps: A lying line means folding the top half onto the bottom half.
B: its top and bottom bumps match.
A, T and V only have a standing line.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up standing (vertical) and lying (horizontal) lines

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does the capital letter H have?
quiz.explain: H matches when folded down the middle and when folded across the middle. That is 2 lines.
steps: Fold H down the middle: the halves match (1 line).
Fold H across the middle: the top and bottom match (2nd line).
So H has 2 lines of symmetry.
quiz.mistake: Finds only one of the two folds

quiz.q: Which of these has the most lines of symmetry?
quiz.explain: Any fold through the centre of a circle makes matching halves, so a circle has endless lines of symmetry.
steps: Any fold through the centre of a circle makes matching halves.
So a circle has endless lines, the most.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the square has the most because it has 4

teach.ask: Gappu folded a paper heart down the middle and both halves matched! What is that fold line called?
teach.praise: Yes! When both halves match after folding, the fold is a line of symmetry. Gappu loves it!
teach.nudge: What happens to the two halves when Gappu folds? What do we call that line?

revise.summary: A line of symmetry cuts a shape into two halves that match exactly when folded. Some shapes have one line of symmetry, some have many and some have none.
focus: Count lines of symmetry of squares, rectangles, triangles and circles
Find letters with standing, lying or no lines of symmetry
remember: Square: 4 lines. Rectangle that is not a square: 2
Triangle with all sides equal: 3. Circle: endless
A, T, V: standing line. B, C, E: lying line. F, L, N, S: none
traps: Don't forget the two corner-to-corner folds of a square
The diagonals of a rectangle are not lines of symmetry
Don't mix up standing (vertical) and lying (horizontal) lines

learn.hook: Drop some paint on paper, fold it, press and open. A butterfly appears! How?
points: Ink-blot design: put paint on one half, fold along the middle, press and open. The paint copies onto the other half like a mirror image.
The fold line is the line of symmetry of the design.
When folding a paper plane, the first middle fold is its line of symmetry. Both wings should match.
Place a mirror on the line of symmetry of half a picture and you see the whole picture.
A symmetrical plane flies straighter. If one wing is bigger, the plane turns or tips over.

example.q: Ritu folds a paper plane but one wing is bigger than the other. What will probably happen when she throws it?
steps: One side pushes on the air more than the other.
So the plane turns or tips instead of flying straight.
example.answer: It will turn or tip to one side

learn.reallife: Rangoli artists, ink-blot painters and paper-plane champions all use a fold line to make matching halves.

games.title: Make an ink-blot design
items: Fold a paper in half and open it
Fold it again along the same line
Open to see the matching halves

games.title: Planes and blots
items: The fold in an ink-blot design is a line of symmetry.
The two halves match across it.
A plane with one big and one small wing flies straight.
Unequal wings make it turn or tip.
A mirror on the line of symmetry shows the whole shape.
The mirror shows the missing half.
In an ink blot, the copy on the other half is exactly the same way round.
It is a mirror image, flipped left to right.
The middle fold of a paper plane helps make both wings equal.
It is the plane's line of symmetry.

quiz.q: In an ink-blot design, what is the fold line called?
quiz.explain: The fold line splits the design into two matching halves.
steps: The fold splits the ink-blot design into two matching halves.
A line that makes matching halves is a line of symmetry.
So the fold line is the line of symmetry.

quiz.q: Paint is put on the left half and the paper is folded. Where does the copy appear?
options: On the right half, flipped like a mirror
quiz.explain: Folding presses the paint onto the other half as a mirror image.
steps: Folding presses the paint from the left half onto the right half.
The copy is a mirror image.
So it appears on the right half, flipped like a mirror.
Answer: On the right half, flipped like a mirror
quiz.mistake: Thinks the copy is not flipped

quiz.q: Why should both wings of a paper plane be the same?
quiz.explain: A symmetrical plane balances and flies straight.
steps: If both wings are the same, the plane is balanced.
A balanced (symmetrical) plane does not pull to one side.
quiz.mistake: Does not link symmetry to balance

quiz.q: Which fold is the line of symmetry of a paper plane?
options: The first fold down the middle
A fold at one wing tip
quiz.explain: The middle fold divides the plane into two equal halves.
steps: A line of symmetry splits the plane into two equal halves.
The first fold down the middle does exactly this.
A fold at a wing tip or the nose is not in the middle.
Answer: The first fold down the middle
quiz.mistake: Picks a fold that is not in the middle

quiz.q: Ankit places a mirror along the middle of half a butterfly drawing. What does he see?
quiz.explain: The mirror shows the other matching half, so the whole butterfly appears.
steps: A mirror on the line of symmetry shows the matching half.
Half a butterfly + its mirror half = a whole butterfly.
So Ankit sees a whole butterfly.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what a mirror shows

quiz.q: An ink-blot design has 6 dots on the left half before folding (none on the fold). How many dots after opening?
quiz.explain: Each dot is copied to the right half: 6 + 6 = 12.
steps: Folding copies each dot onto the right half.

quiz.q: A plane drifts to the left every time. What is likely wrong?
quiz.explain: Unequal (not symmetrical) wings make a plane turn.
steps: If it always drifts one way, its two sides are not the same.
So the wings are not equal.
Answer: The wings are not equal

quiz.q: A mirror is placed on the line of symmetry of half the letter A. What letter do you see?
quiz.explain: The mirror shows the missing half, completing the A.
steps: A has a standing line of symmetry down the middle.
A mirror on that line shows the missing half.
Together they make the whole letter A.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the mirror shows a different letter

teach.ask: Gappu wants to make a butterfly painting with matching wings. Explain how folding helps.
teach.praise: Paint one half, fold and press, and the wings match like a mirror. Beautiful!
teach.nudge: What does folding do to the paint on one half?

revise.summary: In an ink-blot design, paint on one half copies onto the other half as a mirror image, and the fold line is the line of symmetry. A symmetrical paper plane with matching wings flies straighter.
focus: Know what an ink-blot fold makes
Find the line of symmetry of a paper plane
Use a mirror to complete half a picture
remember: The fold line is the line of symmetry of the design
A mirror on the line of symmetry of half a picture shows the whole picture
If one wing is bigger, the plane turns or tips over
traps: The copy is flipped like a mirror, not the same way round
Don't forget the copied dots when counting
Don't make the wings unequal: unequal wings make a plane turn

learn.hook: Put a mirror on half a picture and, like magic, the whole picture appears!
points: A mirror shows a flipped copy. Left becomes right and right becomes left.
If you know one half of a symmetrical shape, you can draw the other half like a mirror image.
Each point on one side is the same distance from the mirror line as its partner on the other side.
Fold paper, cut a shape on the fold and open it. You get a symmetrical shape!
In a mirror, b looks like d.

example.q: Half of a rangoli has 7 dots on the left of the fold line, and no dots on the line. How many dots are in the whole rangoli?
steps: The right half is a mirror copy of the left half.

learn.reallife: Mehendi designs, kite patterns and paper cut-outs for Diwali use mirror halves.

games.title: Mirror magic
items: In a mirror, your right hand looks like a left hand.
A mirror flips left and right.
The letter b looks like d in a mirror held to its side.
The bump flips to the other side.
The mirror half of a shape can be a different size.
Mirror halves are exactly the same size and shape.
If you cut a half-heart on a fold and open the paper, you get a whole heart.
The fold is the line of symmetry.
The word MOM looks the same in a mirror held to its side.
M and O look the same flipped, and the word reads the same both ways.
The letter F looks the same in a mirror held to its side.
F faces the other way in the mirror.

items.text: Left half has 5 petals and none are on the line. The whole flower has ___ petals.

In a mirror held to the side, the letter d looks like ___.

quiz.q: Riya folds a paper in half and cuts out half a heart along the fold. What does she get when she opens it?
quiz.explain: The fold is the line of symmetry. Opening it shows both matching halves joined: a whole heart.
steps: The fold is the line of symmetry.
Cutting half a heart on the fold cuts both layers at once.
Opening it shows both halves joined: a whole heart.
quiz.mistake: Does not see that the fold joins the two halves

quiz.q: In a mirror held to its side, what does the letter b look like?
quiz.explain: A mirror flips left and right. The bump of b moves to the left side, making it look like d.
steps: A mirror held to the side flips left and right.
The bump of b is on the right; in the mirror it moves to the left.
quiz.mistake: Flips it upside down instead of left to right

quiz.q: A symmetrical rangoli has 7 dots on the left of the fold line and none on the line. How many dots are in the whole rangoli?
quiz.explain: The right half is a mirror copy, so it has 7 dots too. 7 + 7 = 14.
steps: The right half is a mirror copy of the left half.

quiz.q: Which word looks the same in a mirror held to its side?
quiz.explain: M and O look the same when flipped, and MOM reads the same both ways. B, D, S, N and P do not.
steps: A word stays the same in a side mirror if each letter is symmetrical and the word reads the same both ways.
M and O are symmetrical, and MOM reads the same backwards.
B, D, S, N and P flip, so the answer is MOM.
quiz.mistake: Checks only one letter of the word

quiz.q: Which digit looks the same in a mirror held to its side?
quiz.explain: 8 has a standing line of symmetry, so its mirror image is the same. 2, 4 and 7 face the other way.
steps: A side mirror flips left and right.
8 has a standing line of symmetry, so it looks the same.
2, 4 and 7 face the other way in a mirror.
quiz.mistake: Does not picture the digit flipped left to right

quiz.q: Arjun draws the left half of a symmetrical shape. It is 3 squares wide. How wide is the full shape?
quiz.explain: The right half is the same width as the left half. 3 + 3 = 6 squares.
steps: The right half is the same width as the left half.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the half is already the whole shape

quiz.q: A dot is 4 squares to the left of a mirror line. Where is its mirror dot?
options: 4 squares to the right of the line
4 squares to the left of the line
8 squares to the right of the line
quiz.explain: A mirror dot is the same distance from the line but on the other side.
steps: A mirror dot is the same distance from the line, but on the other side.
The dot is 4 squares to the left.
So its mirror dot is 4 squares to the right.
Answer: 4 squares to the right of the line
quiz.mistake: Doubles the distance instead of keeping it the same

quiz.q: Kabir stands 2 steps in front of a mirror. How far behind the mirror does his image seem to be?
quiz.explain: Your mirror image always seems to be the same distance behind the mirror as you are in front of it.
steps: An image seems as far behind a mirror as you are in front of it.
So his image seems 2 steps behind.

teach.praise: Magic! Put the mirror on the line and the other half appears, the same but flipped. Gappu's butterfly is complete!
teach.nudge: What does a mirror do to a picture? How is the other half related to the first half?

Use equal distance from the mirror line

topics.title: Holes and cuts: predict the pattern

learn.hook: Fold a paper twice, snip a corner, and open it. Will you get one hole or four?
points: Folding once makes 2 layers. A cut away from the fold makes 2 holes; a cut on the fold makes 1 hole.
Folding twice makes 4 layers. A cut in the middle (away from all folds) makes 4 holes.
A cut at the corner where both folds meet makes 1 hole in the centre of the paper.
A cut on just one folded edge (not the corner) makes 2 holes.
To get a square hole, fold twice and cut straight across the folded corner, the same distance along both folds.

example.q: A paper is folded twice. A small half-circle is cut on one folded edge, away from the corner. How many holes after opening?
steps: On a fold, the 4 layers pair up into 2 holes.

learn.reallife: Paper snowflakes and paper lanterns for Diwali are made by folding and cutting. The more folds, the more holes!

games.title: Cut and count the holes
pairs: 1 fold, cut away from the fold
2 folds, cut at the folded corner

games.title: Predict the cut
items: Each fold doubles the layers: 2, then 4.
One fold and a cut away from the fold gives 1 hole.
The cut goes through 2 layers, so 2 holes.
Cutting straight across the twice-folded corner can make a square hole.
The 4 corner pieces open into a square.
A half-circle cut on the fold opens into a full circle.
The two halves join at the fold.

quiz.q: A paper folded once has a half-circle cut on the fold. What do you see when you open it?
quiz.explain: The half-circle on the fold opens into one full circle.
steps: The half-circle is cut on the fold.
When opened, its mirror half appears on the other side.
The two halves join into 1 circle hole.

quiz.q: A paper folded once has a small hole punched away from the fold. How many holes after opening?
quiz.explain: The punch goes through 2 layers, so 2 holes.
steps: A paper folded once has 2 layers.
A punch away from the fold goes through both layers.

quiz.q: A paper folded twice has a hole punched in the middle, away from all folds. How many holes after opening?
quiz.explain: Two folds make 4 layers, so 4 holes.

quiz.q: A paper is folded twice and a quarter circle is cut at the corner where both folds meet. What do you get?
quiz.explain: The 4 quarter circles join into one circle in the middle.
steps: Folding twice makes 4 layers that meet at the folded corner.
The quarter circle at that corner is copied into 4 quarters.
The 4 quarters join into 1 circle in the centre.
quiz.mistake: Thinks each layer gives a separate hole

quiz.q: How many layers are there after folding a paper 3 times?
quiz.explain: Each fold doubles the layers: 2, 4, 8.

quiz.q: Maya wants a square hole in the centre. What should she do?
options: Fold twice and cut straight across the folded corner
Fold once and cut a circle
quiz.explain: A straight cut across the twice-folded corner opens into a square.
steps: To get one hole in the centre, cut at the corner where the folds meet.
Fold twice, then cut straight across the folded corner.
The 4 small triangles open into one square hole.
Answer: Fold twice and cut straight across the folded corner

quiz.q: A paper is folded once. On the fold, Ravi cuts a rectangle 1 cm wide (from the fold) and 2 cm long (along the fold). What hole does he get?
quiz.explain: The 1 cm width doubles to 2 cm when opened, so the hole is 2 cm by 2 cm, a square.
steps: The rectangle is cut on the fold, so its width doubles when opened.
1 cm from the fold → 1 + 1 = 2 cm wide. Length along the fold stays 2 cm.
So the hole is 2 cm by 2 cm, a square.
Answer: A 2 cm by 2 cm square

quiz.q: A paper folded twice has a small notch cut on one folded edge, not at the corner. How many notches or holes after opening?
quiz.explain: The 4 layers pair up across the fold, making 2 holes.
steps: A notch on a folded edge cuts layers in pairs that are joined across that fold.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every cut on 4 layers gives 4

teach.ask: Gappu folded paper twice and punched one hole in the middle. Gappu expected 1 hole but got 4. Explain.
teach.praise: Two folds make 4 layers, so one punch makes 4 holes! Now I can predict.
teach.nudge: How many layers does the paper have after two folds?

revise.summary: Folding paper makes layers, so one cut can make several holes. A cut on a fold opens into one hole, while a cut away from the folds goes through every layer.
focus: Count layers after folding
Predict how many holes a cut makes
Plan a cut to get a square hole
remember: Fold once: 2 layers. Fold twice: 4 layers. Fold 3 times: 8 layers
Folded twice: cut in the middle makes 4 holes; cut at the corner where both folds meet makes 1 hole
A cut on just one folded edge makes 2 holes
traps: Don't forget the layer underneath
Each fold doubles the layers; don't add 2
Don't keep the width cut from the fold the same; it doubles when opened

learn.hook: The word AMBULANCE is written back to front on the van. Why? Look in a car's mirror!
points: Place a mirror on a shape. If the shape and its reflection make the same shape, the mirror is on a line of symmetry.
Digits like 0, 1 and 8 look the same in a mirror held beside them.
A mirror also reverses the order of digits. So only numbers like 88, 101 and 808 look the same in the mirror.
AMBULANCE is written in mirror writing on the front of the van so drivers ahead can read it in their rear-view mirror.
You can try mirror writing in any script: write each letter flipped, starting from the other side.

example.q: Does 18 look the same in a mirror held beside it?
steps: 1 and 8 look the same in a mirror.
But the mirror swaps their order: 18 looks like 81.
So 18 does not look the same.

learn.reallife: Next time you see an ambulance, look at the front. The writing is reversed for the mirrors of cars in front!

games.title: Looks the same in a mirror held beside it?

items.text: AMBULANCE is reversed so drivers read it in their ___.
In a mirror, 18 looks like ___.
The digit ___ looks the same in a mirror.
Mirror writing starts from the ___ side.

quiz.q: Which number looks exactly the same in a mirror held beside it?
quiz.explain: 8 and 0 look the same in a mirror, and 808 reads the same from both ends.
steps: A side mirror reverses the order of digits and flips each one.
8 and 0 look the same flipped, and 808 reads the same from both ends.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the mirror reverses the order

quiz.q: Why is AMBULANCE written in mirror writing on the van?
options: So only children can read it
So drivers ahead can read it in their mirrors
quiz.explain: A rear-view mirror flips the writing back to normal.
steps: A rear-view mirror flips writing left to right.
Mirror writing on the van flips back to normal in the mirror.
So drivers ahead can read AMBULANCE in their mirrors.
Answer: So drivers ahead can read it in their mirrors
quiz.mistake: Does not know how mirrors flip words

quiz.q: How does the number 18 look in a mirror held beside it?
quiz.explain: 1 and 8 stay the same, but the order is reversed: 81.
steps: 1 and 8 each look the same in a mirror.
But a side mirror reverses the order.

quiz.q: Which word looks the same in a mirror held beside it?
quiz.explain: W and O look the same in a mirror, and WOW reads the same both ways.
steps: W and O are symmetrical letters.
BOOK, PEN and SUN have letters that flip, so the answer is WOW.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word with non-symmetric letters

quiz.q: Hema puts a mirror across a heart shape. The heart and its reflection make the same heart. Where is the mirror?
quiz.explain: When a mirror shows the same shape, it is on the line of symmetry.
steps: The mirror shows the same heart only if it splits the heart into matching halves.
A line that splits a shape into matching halves is the line of symmetry.
So the mirror is on the line of symmetry.
Answer: On the line of symmetry
quiz.mistake: Does not link the mirror to symmetry

quiz.q: Which number made of 1s and 0s looks the same in a mirror?
quiz.explain: 1001 reads the same from both ends, and 1 and 0 look the same in a mirror.
steps: 1 and 0 look the same in a mirror, but the order is reversed.

quiz.q: Which of these digits does NOT look the same in a mirror held beside it?
quiz.explain: 3 flips and faces the other way. 0, 8 and 1 stay the same.
steps: 0, 1 and 8 have a standing line of symmetry, so they look the same.
3 has no standing line of symmetry.
In a mirror, 3 faces the other way.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all digits stay the same

quiz.q: Sunil writes his name in mirror writing. How should he write?
options: Flip each letter and start from the other side
quiz.explain: Mirror writing flips each letter left to right and reverses the order.
steps: A mirror flips left to right.
So each letter is flipped, and the order runs from the other side.
Flip each letter and start from the other side.
Answer: Flip each letter and start from the other side
quiz.mistake: Thinks mirror writing is upside down

teach.ask: Gappu wrote 18 and looked in the mirror. Gappu saw 81 and got confused. Explain.
teach.praise: The mirror swaps the order! Only numbers like 88 or 808 look the same.
teach.nudge: What does a mirror do to the order of digits?

revise.summary: If a shape and its mirror reflection make the same shape, the mirror is on a line of symmetry. A mirror flips digits and also reverses their order.
focus: Find numbers and words that look the same in a mirror
Know why AMBULANCE is in mirror writing
Write in mirror writing
remember: 0, 1 and 8 look the same in a mirror held beside them
Only numbers like 88, 101 and 808 look the same in the mirror
AMBULANCE is reversed so drivers ahead can read it in their rear-view mirror
traps: Don't forget the mirror reverses the order: 18 looks like 81
Not all digits stay the same: 3 faces the other way
Mirror writing is not upside down

topics.title: Symmetry of regular shapes on a dot grid

learn.hook: A regular pentagon has 5 equal sides and 5 lines of symmetry. Coincidence? Let's check other shapes!
points: A regular shape has all sides equal and all angles equal.
Regular triangle: 3 lines of symmetry. Square: 4. Regular pentagon: 5. Regular hexagon: 6.
For a regular shape, the number of lines of symmetry equals the number of sides.
A rectangle that is not a square has only 2. A shape like a kite has 1.
On a dot grid, draw a shape and then test each possible fold line to find its lines of symmetry.

example.q: A regular hexagon has 6 equal sides. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
steps: For a regular shape, lines = sides.

learn.reallife: Floor tiles, road signs and honeycombs often use regular shapes because they look balanced from every side.

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a regular pentagon have?
quiz.explain: A regular pentagon has 5 equal sides and 5 lines of symmetry.
steps: For regular shapes, lines of symmetry = number of sides.
So it has 5 lines of symmetry.

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a regular hexagon have?
quiz.explain: Regular shapes have as many lines of symmetry as sides.
steps: For regular shapes, lines of symmetry = number of sides.
So 6 lines (3 through corners, 3 through middles of sides).

quiz.q: A square has 4 sides. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
quiz.explain: 2 lines through the middles of sides and 2 diagonals: 4.
steps: 2 lines through the middles of opposite sides.

quiz.q: Which shape has exactly 2 lines of symmetry?
options: A rectangle that is not a square
quiz.explain: A rectangle folds in half across and along, but not on its diagonals.
steps: Square: 4 lines. Regular triangle: 3. Circle: endless.
A rectangle (not a square) folds evenly across and along, but not on its diagonals.
Answer: A rectangle that is not a square
quiz.mistake: Thinks the diagonals of a rectangle are lines of symmetry

quiz.q: A regular octagon has 8 equal sides. How many lines of symmetry?
quiz.explain: For regular shapes, lines of symmetry = number of sides.
steps: For regular shapes, lines of symmetry = number of sides.

quiz.q: On a dot grid, Sara draws a kite shape. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
quiz.explain: A kite folds into matching halves only along its long middle line.
steps: A kite has two pairs of equal sides next to each other.
It folds into matching halves only along its long middle line.
quiz.mistake: Thinks it has 2 like a rectangle

quiz.q: Which is true for regular shapes?
options: Lines of symmetry = double the sides
Lines of symmetry = number of sides
They have no lines of symmetry
quiz.explain: Triangle 3, square 4, pentagon 5, hexagon 6.
steps: Check examples: triangle 3 sides, 3 lines; square 4, 4; pentagon 5, 5; hexagon 6, 6.
So lines of symmetry = number of sides.
Answer: Lines of symmetry = number of sides

quiz.q: How many more lines of symmetry does a regular hexagon have than a regular triangle?
steps: Regular hexagon: 6 lines. Regular triangle: 3 lines.

teach.ask: Gappu found a regular pentagon tile and wants to know how many ways it can be folded into matching halves. Explain.
teach.praise: A regular pentagon has 5 sides, so 5 lines of symmetry!
teach.nudge: What is the link between sides and lines of symmetry in regular shapes?

revise.summary: A regular shape has all sides equal and all angles equal. For a regular shape, the number of lines of symmetry equals the number of sides.
focus: Count lines of symmetry of regular shapes
Compare with rectangles and kites
Test fold lines on a dot grid
remember: Regular triangle 3, square 4, regular pentagon 5, regular hexagon 6
Lines of symmetry = number of sides (regular shapes)
Rectangle that is not a square: 2. Kite: 1
traps: Don't forget the diagonals of a square
The diagonals of a rectangle are not lines of symmetry
Don't halve the number of sides

learn.hook: Look at a bathroom wall. The same tile design repeats again and again. Can you find the smallest piece that repeats?
points: A tile pattern repeats a basic unit again and again.
To continue the pattern, find the unit and repeat it in the same way.
A tile can be slid (moved without turning), flipped (like a mirror) or turned (rotated) to make patterns.
A quarter turn rotates a tile by one right angle. Four quarter turns bring it back to the start.

example.q: A border goes ▲▼▲▼▲▼. What is the repeating unit, and which move changes ▲ into ▼?
steps: ▼ is ▲ flipped upside down (or turned half a turn).
example.answer: Unit ▲▼; a flip or half turn

learn.reallife: Sarees, bangles, temple floors and school walls all have tile patterns made by sliding, flipping or turning one design.

quiz.q: In the pattern ■●■●■●, what is the repeating unit?
quiz.explain: ■● repeats again and again.
steps: Look for the smallest part that repeats.

quiz.q: A tile is moved to the right without turning or flipping. What is this move called?
quiz.explain: Moving without turning is a slide.
steps: The tile only moves; it does not turn or flip.
That kind of move is called a slide.

quiz.q: A tile with an arrow → becomes ← . Which single move could do this?
quiz.explain: Flipping like a mirror changes → to ←. A half turn does too.
steps: A slide keeps → pointing the same way.
A quarter turn makes → point up or down.
A flip (mirror) or a half turn makes → point ←.
Answer: A flip (or a half turn)

quiz.q: How many quarter turns bring a tile back to how it started?
quiz.explain: 4 quarter turns make a full turn.
steps: One full turn brings the tile back to how it started.
A full turn is 4 quarter turns.

quiz.q: What comes next? ▲▲▼▲▲▼▲▲
quiz.explain: The unit is ▲▲▼, so after ▲▲ comes ▼.
steps: The pattern ends with ▲▲ from a new unit.

quiz.q: In ⭐🌙🌙⭐🌙🌙, how many shapes are in the repeating unit?
quiz.explain: ⭐🌙🌙 has 3 shapes.

quiz.q: A tile is turned a quarter turn each time: ↑ then →. What comes next?
quiz.explain: Each quarter turn moves the arrow one right angle clockwise: ↑, →, ↓, ←.
steps: A quarter turn clockwise moves the arrow one right angle: ↑ then →, then ↓, then ←.

quiz.q: A floor border uses the unit 🟥🟨🟨. How many 🟨 tiles are in 4 units?
quiz.explain: Each unit has 2 yellow tiles. 4 × 2 = 8.

teach.ask: Gappu wants to tile a wall border with a pattern. Explain how to make one using a single tile.
teach.praise: I picked a unit and slid, flipped or turned it again and again. My border is ready!
teach.nudge: What do you repeat, and what moves can you use?

revise.summary: A tile pattern repeats a basic unit again and again. A tile can be slid, flipped or turned to make patterns.
focus: Find the repeating unit and continue a pattern
Name slide, flip and turn moves
Use quarter turns
remember: Slide: move without turning. Flip: like a mirror. Turn: rotate
A quarter turn rotates a tile by one right angle
Four quarter turns bring it back to the start
traps: Don't pick only one part as the unit
A slide does not change direction
2 quarter turns are not a full turn

learn.hook: Bees build honeycombs with hexagons that fit perfectly. Why not circles?
points: Tessellation means covering a surface with shapes that leave no gaps and do not overlap.
Squares, rectangles, regular triangles and regular hexagons tessellate on their own.
Circles and regular pentagons leave gaps, so they do not tessellate on their own.
Some tiles in a shop are symmetrical, some are not. Look for a line of symmetry in each tile design.
You can join shapes to make a new tile that tessellates, or design your own tile with cut-outs or a rangoli kit.

example.q: Can circular tiles cover a floor without gaps?
steps: There are curved gaps between them.

learn.reallife: Look at floors, footpaths and walls. Paver blocks and tiles fit together like a puzzle with no gaps!

games.title: Tessellation facts
items: Tiles in a tessellation may overlap.
Hexagons fit together with no gaps.
Two regular triangles joined make a shape that also tessellates.
They make a rhombus, which tessellates.
Every tile design in a shop is symmetrical.
Some designs have no line of symmetry.

quiz.q: What does tessellation mean?
options: Covering a surface with shapes with no gaps and no overlaps
quiz.explain: Tessellating shapes fit together completely.
steps: Tessellation means shapes fitting together over a surface.
They must leave no gaps and must not overlap.
So: covering a surface with shapes with no gaps and no overlaps.
Answer: Covering a surface with shapes with no gaps and no overlaps

quiz.q: Which shape does NOT tessellate on its own?
quiz.explain: Circles leave gaps between them.
steps: Squares, rectangles and regular hexagons fit together with no gaps.
So circles leave gaps and do not tessellate.

quiz.q: Which shape do bees use in honeycombs?
quiz.explain: Regular hexagons fit together with no gaps.
steps: A honeycomb is made of six-sided cells.
Regular hexagons fit together with no gaps.
quiz.mistake: Picks a shape that leaves gaps

quiz.q: Two regular triangles are joined side to side. Does the new tile tessellate?
quiz.explain: They make a rhombus, which fits with copies of itself.
steps: Two regular triangles joined side to side make a rhombus.
Copies of a rhombus fit together with no gaps or overlaps.

quiz.q: A tile shows a flower with 4 equal petals. Is it symmetrical?
quiz.explain: A flower with 4 equal petals has lines of symmetry.
steps: A flower with 4 equal petals can be folded so the halves match.
It has lines of symmetry through the petals.
quiz.mistake: Does not look for a fold line

quiz.q: Which is true about a regular pentagon?
options: It leaves gaps when tiled alone
quiz.explain: Regular pentagons do not fit together without gaps.
steps: A regular pentagon has 5 sides, not 4.
When copies are placed together, gaps are left between them.
So it leaves gaps when tiled alone.
Answer: It leaves gaps when tiled alone

quiz.q: A floor is covered by 6 rows of 8 square tiles with no gaps. How many tiles?
steps: 6 rows with 8 tiles in each row.

quiz.q: Leena makes her own tile using a rangoli kit. What must be true for it to tile a floor?
options: Copies fit together with no gaps or overlaps
quiz.explain: A tessellating tile fits with its copies, leaving no gaps.
steps: A tile covers a floor only if copies fit with no gaps.
Colour and size do not matter.
Answer: Copies fit together with no gaps or overlaps

teach.ask: Gappu wants round tiles for the classroom floor. Explain why that may be a problem.
teach.praise: Round tiles leave gaps! Squares or hexagons fit perfectly.
teach.nudge: What happens between circles when you put them side by side?

revise.summary: Tessellation means covering a surface with shapes that leave no gaps and do not overlap. Squares, rectangles, regular triangles and regular hexagons tessellate; circles and regular pentagons do not.
focus: Know what tessellation means
Tell which shapes tessellate on their own
Design a tile that tessellates
remember: Tessellation: no gaps, no overlaps
Tessellate on their own: squares, rectangles, regular triangles, regular hexagons
Circles and regular pentagons leave gaps
traps: Tessellation is not symmetry
Not every regular shape tessellates
Don't think joined shapes cannot tessellate; they still can

topics.title: Floor patterns and the catty wall

learn.hook: Cut a bump from one side of a square and stick it on the opposite side. You get a cat-shaped tile that still fits!
points: A floor pattern is made by repeating one tessellating tile again and again.
Catty-wall trick: cut a piece from one side of a square and slide it to the opposite side.
The new tile has a funny shape (like a cat), but copies still fit together with no gaps.
The area stays the same, because nothing was thrown away: the piece only moved.
If the piece is not slid exactly to the opposite side, the tiles will not fit.

example.q: Raghav cuts a small triangle from the bottom of a square tile and sticks it on the top. Will copies fit together?
steps: The bump on top matches the gap at the bottom of the tile above.
So copies fit with no gaps or overlaps.

learn.reallife: Artists make animal-shaped tiles, like birds and fish, using this trick. Some famous tiles look like lizards!

games.title: Make a catty-wall tile
items: Cut a shape from one side
Slide the piece to the opposite side
Repeat the tile to cover the wall

games.title: Catty-wall facts
items: Sliding the cut piece to the opposite side keeps the tile tessellating.
The bump fits the gap of the next tile.
The new tile has a bigger area than the square.
The piece was only moved, so the area stays the same.
You can stick the piece anywhere and it will still fit.
It must go exactly opposite where it was cut.
A floor pattern repeats one tile again and again.
If made by cutting and sliding, they fit together.

quiz.q: In the catty-wall trick, where does the cut piece go?
quiz.explain: The piece is slid to the opposite side so the tiles still fit.
steps: A piece is cut from one side of the square.
It is slid to the opposite side and stuck there.
So the piece goes to the opposite side.

quiz.q: After the catty-wall trick, how does the tile's area compare with the square's?
quiz.explain: Nothing is added or removed; a piece is only moved.
steps: Nothing is thrown away and nothing is added.
So the area stays the same as the square's.

quiz.q: Why do the new cat-shaped tiles still fit together?
options: The bump on one side fills the gap on the next tile
quiz.explain: Each bump matches a gap, so there are no gaps or overlaps.
steps: Each tile has a bump on one side and a gap on the opposite side.
The bump of one tile fills the gap of the next tile.
So they fit with no gaps or overlaps.
Answer: The bump on one side fills the gap on the next tile
quiz.mistake: Does not see bumps and gaps match

quiz.q: What is a floor pattern made by?
options: Repeating one tile with no gaps
quiz.explain: A floor pattern repeats a tessellating tile.
steps: A floor pattern covers the floor fully.
It repeats one tile that fits with no gaps.
So: repeating one tile with no gaps.
Answer: Repeating one tile with no gaps

quiz.q: Tanu cuts a piece from the left side of a square and sticks it on the TOP. What may happen?
options: The tiles may not fit together
quiz.explain: The piece must slide to the opposite side (right). Moving it elsewhere breaks the fit.
steps: In the catty-wall trick, a piece cut from the left must slide to the right.
Sticking it on the top breaks the match of bumps and gaps.
So the tiles may not fit together.
Answer: The tiles may not fit together

quiz.q: A wall needs 5 rows of 7 catty tiles. How many tiles?
steps: 5 rows with 7 tiles in each row.

quiz.q: A square tile has area 16 small squares. After the catty-wall trick, what is its area?
quiz.explain: Moving a piece does not change the area.
steps: The catty-wall trick only moves a piece; nothing is added or removed.
So the area does not change.
quiz.mistake: Adds or takes away the piece

quiz.q: Which shape is the best start for a catty-wall tile?
quiz.explain: Squares tessellate, so a cut-and-slide square still tessellates.
steps: Squares tessellate; circles, regular pentagons and ovals leave gaps.
quiz.mistake: Picks a shape that does not tessellate

teach.ask: Gappu wants a wall full of cat-shaped tiles that fit with no gaps. How can Gappu make the tile?
teach.praise: Cut a bit from a square and slide it to the opposite side! Meow, it fits!
teach.nudge: Where must the cut piece go so the tiles still fit?

revise.summary: A floor pattern repeats one tessellating tile. In the catty-wall trick, cut a piece from one side of a square and slide it to the opposite side; copies still fit and the area stays the same.
focus: Make a catty-wall tile
Know why the new tiles still fit
Know that moving a piece does not change area
remember: Slide the cut piece to the opposite side
The area stays the same because the piece only moved
The bump on one side fills the gap on the next tile
traps: Don't throw the cut piece away
Moving the piece to a side that is not opposite breaks the fit
Changing shape does not change the area here

learn.hook: Look closely at a butterfly, a peepal leaf or a hibiscus flower. Nature loves symmetry!
points: Many living things are symmetrical: a butterfly's wings match, and many leaves match on both sides of the middle vein.
Some leaves are not symmetrical, like a torn leaf or a leaf with uneven sides.
Sort leaves into symmetrical and non-symmetrical by folding them along the middle vein.
Flowers with equal petals, like a 5-petal hibiscus, can have several lines of symmetry.
Use leaves and flowers dipped in paint to make prints for designs and greeting cards.

example.q: A flower has 5 equal petals evenly spread. How many lines of symmetry might it have?
steps: Like a regular pentagon, a line can go through each petal.

learn.reallife: On a nature walk, collect fallen leaves and flowers. Fold them to test symmetry, then print them on a Diwali card!

games.title: Nature symmetry
items: Its body is the line of symmetry.
The middle vein of a leaf is often its line of symmetry.
The two halves match across it.
Leaf prints can be used to make greeting cards.
Paint the leaf and press it on paper.
A flower with 4 equal petals has no line of symmetry.
It has lines of symmetry through the petals.

quiz.q: Which part of a butterfly is its line of symmetry?
quiz.explain: The body divides the butterfly into two matching halves.
steps: The line of symmetry divides the butterfly into two matching halves.
The body runs down the middle.
So the body is the line of symmetry.
Answer: Its body down the middle
quiz.mistake: Picks a part on one side

quiz.q: How can you test if a leaf is symmetrical?
options: Fold it along the middle vein and see if the halves match
quiz.explain: If the halves match when folded, it is symmetrical.
steps: A shape is symmetrical if both halves match when folded.
Fold the leaf along its middle vein.
If the halves match, it is symmetrical.
Answer: Fold it along the middle vein and see if the halves match
quiz.mistake: Does not know how to test

quiz.q: Which is most likely NOT symmetrical?
options: A leaf torn on one side
quiz.explain: The torn side no longer matches the other side.
steps: Flowers, butterflies and peepal leaves have matching halves.
A leaf torn on one side no longer matches the other side.
So the torn leaf is most likely NOT symmetrical.
Answer: A leaf torn on one side

quiz.q: A flower has 6 equal petals evenly spread. How many lines of symmetry can it have?
quiz.explain: Like a regular hexagon, it has 6 lines of symmetry.
steps: 6 equal petals, evenly spread, are like a regular hexagon.
A regular hexagon has 6 lines of symmetry.
So the flower can have 6 lines.

quiz.q: Riya collects 12 leaves. 9 are symmetrical. How many are not?
To make a leaf print card, what should you do?
options: Paint a leaf and press it on paper
quiz.explain: Painting and pressing makes a print.
steps: A print is made by pressing paint onto paper.
Paint a leaf and press it on paper.
Burning, throwing or tearing does not make a print.
Answer: Paint a leaf and press it on paper

quiz.q: A leaf print is made on one half of a folded card and the card is pressed shut. What appears on the other half?
options: A mirror image of the print
quiz.explain: The wet paint copies as a mirror image, like an ink blot.
steps: The wet paint presses onto the other half when the card is shut.
Like an ink blot, the copy is flipped.
So a mirror image of the print appears.
Answer: A mirror image of the print
quiz.mistake: Does not connect it with ink-blot designs

quiz.q: Which animal shows symmetry when seen from the front?
quiz.explain: A tiger's face has matching left and right halves.
steps: A tiger's face has matching left and right halves.
A snail shell and coiled rope are spirals; a broken shell is uneven.
So a tiger's face shows symmetry.

teach.ask: Gappu found a leaf on a nature walk. How can Gappu check if it is symmetrical, and what can Gappu make with it?
teach.praise: Fold along the middle vein: the halves match! Now I will print it on a card.
teach.nudge: How do you test the leaf, and what can you make from it?

revise.summary: Many living things are symmetrical, like butterfly wings and many leaves, but some are not. Test a leaf by folding it along the middle vein.
focus: Find lines of symmetry in nature
Sort leaves into symmetrical and non-symmetrical
Know how leaf prints make mirror images
remember: Fold a leaf along the middle vein to test symmetry
Flowers with equal petals can have several lines of symmetry: 5 equal petals, 5 lines
A butterfly's body down the middle is its line of symmetry

learn.hook: Your birthday is coming! How many days to wait? The calendar knows!
points: A week has 7 days. A year has 12 months.
April, June, September and November have 30 days. February has 28 days (29 in a leap year). All the other months have 31 days.
A year has 365 days. A leap year has 366 days.
The same day of the week comes again every 7 days. If 1 June is a Monday, so are 8, 15, 22 and 29 June.
To count days to a date in the next month, count to the end of this month, then add the days of the next month.

example.q: Today is 28 March. Aisha's birthday is on 5 April. How many days does she have to wait?
steps: March has 31 days. From 28 March to 31 March is 31 - 28 = 3 days.
Then 5 more days to reach 5 April.

learn.reallife: We use calendars to plan holidays, mark exams, count days to Diwali and remember birthdays.

games.title: Calendar facts
items: February gets an extra day, the 29th.
If 1 June is a Monday, then 8 June is also a Monday.
In a year that is not a leap year, February has 28 days.
Only a leap year gives February 29 days.

quiz.q: How many days are there in March?
quiz.explain: March is one of the months with 31 days.
steps: Months with 31 days: January, March, May, July, August, October, December.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up March with a 30-day month

quiz.q: In a year that is not a leap year, how many days does February have?
quiz.explain: February is the shortest month. It has 28 days, and 29 only in a leap year.
steps: In an ordinary year it has 28 days; only in a leap year does it have 29.
quiz.mistake: Gives the leap-year number of days

quiz.q: How many days are there in a year that is not a leap year?
quiz.explain: An ordinary year has 365 days. A leap year has 366.

quiz.q: 1 June is a Monday. What day is 8 June?
quiz.explain: 8 June is 7 days after 1 June. The day of the week repeats every 7 days, so it is Monday again.

quiz.q: Today is Friday. What day will it be 3 days from today?
quiz.explain: Count on: Saturday (1), Sunday (2), Monday (3).
steps: Count on from Friday, not counting today.
quiz.mistake: Counts today as one of the 3 days

quiz.q: How many weeks are there in 28 days?
quiz.explain: Each week has 7 days. 28 ÷ 7 = 4 weeks.
quiz.mistake: Takes away 7 from 28 instead of dividing

quiz.q: Today is 28 March. Aisha's birthday is on 5 April. How many days does she have to wait?
quiz.explain: 28 March to 31 March is 3 days, then 5 more days to 5 April. 3 + 5 = 8 days.

quiz.q: Which of these months has 30 days?
quiz.explain: April has 30 days. May, January and August each have 31 days.
steps: Months with 30 days: April, June, September, November.
May, January and August have 31 days.

teach.ask: Today is 25 May and Gappu's party is on 2 June. Gappu thinks it's 7 days away. How do we count?
teach.praise: Yes! May has 31 days: 25 to 31 is 6 days, then 2 more makes 8 days. Gappu is excited!
teach.nudge: How many days does May have? Count to the end of May first.

revise.summary: A week has 7 days and a year has 12 months. Months have 30 or 31 days, except February with 28 (29 in a leap year), and the same weekday comes again every 7 days.
focus: Know how many days each month has
Find the weekday a few days or weeks later
Count days to a date in the next month
remember: April, June, September and November have 30 days. February has 28 (29 in a leap year). The rest have 31
A year has 365 days; a leap year has 366
If 1 June is a Monday, so are 8, 15, 22 and 29 June
traps: Don't think March has 30 days
Don't count today as one of the days
Not every month has 30 days (12 × 30 = 360 is wrong)

learn.hook: Some children have a birthday on 29 February. They get a real birthday only once in 4 years!
points: A leap year comes every 4 years. It has 366 days because February gets a 29th day.
An ordinary year has 365 days.
2024 was a leap year. Add 4 for the next ones: 2028, 2032. Take away 4 for earlier ones: 2020, 2016.

Many festivals and special days come in fixed months: Republic Day in January, Independence Day in August, Teachers' Day in September, Gandhi Jayanti in October, Children's Day in November, Christmas in December.

example.q: 2024 is a leap year. Which are the next two leap years?

learn.reallife: Calendars help us plan holidays and festivals. Your school calendar marks Republic Day and Independence Day every year.

quiz.q: How many days are there in a leap year?
quiz.explain: A leap year has one extra day, 29 February: 365 + 1 = 366.
steps: A leap year has 1 extra day, 29 February.

quiz.q: 2024 was a leap year. Which year is the next leap year?
quiz.explain: Leap years come every 4 years: 2024 + 4 = 2028.

quiz.q: 2024 was a leap year. Which year was the leap year before it?
